target.title: fix(plugins): quarantine managed npm projects with missing integrity
target.body:
Closes #106604

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where managed npm plugin repair could enter a permanent startup loop when `package-lock.json` recorded the installed plugin without an `integrity` field. Operators then saw `integrity unknown` verification failures, gateway startup migration refused to report ready, and channels stayed down until the poisoned staging project was deleted by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Missing lockfile integrity is treated as a recoverable poisoned managed-project state, not as a permanent content mismatch. On the first such failure the installer quarantines rebuild artifacts (`node_modules` / lockfiles) and retries install once so npm can record integrity from a clean tree. Present-but-different integrity values still fail closed. No new config keys, doctor migrations, or startup-gate policy changes.

Fix quality: compatibility — one-shot recovery on existing managed npm projects without dual readers; performance — recovery only on missing integrity, not every install; usability — clearer recovery path and warning instead of endless crash-loop; security — real integrity mismatches remain fail-closed.

## User Impact

After this fix, a managed plugin project whose lockfile lost integrity metadata recovers automatically on the next install/repair attempt instead of blocking gateway readiness forever. Genuine integrity mismatches still fail and do not install.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Focused Vitest:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts -t "integrity|quarantine|drift from verified"
```

Result: 5 passed (including new regression and existing real-mismatch fail-closed coverage).

Additional focused retest:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts -t "quarantines and rebuilds when package-lock omits integrity"
```

Result: 1 passed.

Static: `git diff --check` clean on touched files. Path-scoped format binary was unavailable in this checkout (`oxfmt` not linked); formatting matches surrounding install code style.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: managed npm install/repair no longer hard-fails forever when package-lock omits integrity; it quarantines once and rebuilds so integrity can be recorded.
- Environment: local macOS OpenClaw checkout; Vitest harness with mocked npm install/lock writes in `src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts`.
- Current-main contrast: on main, `resolveInstalledNpmResolutionMismatch` treats missing `installed.integrity` vs expected integrity as a hard mismatch and rolls back, which re-enters the same poisoned staging state on the next startup repair.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts -t "quarantines and rebuilds when package-lock omits integrity"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts -t "rejects npm installs when the installed artifact drifts from verified metadata"`
- Evidence after fix: new test forces first managed install lock write without integrity, asserts install recovers (ok), quarantine dir is created, and install succeeds; sibling drift test still fails closed on `sha512-evil` vs `sha512-safe`.
- Control check: only the missing-integrity path recovers; present-but-wrong integrity still rejects and leaves the package uninstalled.
- Observed result after fix: missing-integrity install attempt succeeds after one quarantine rebuild; real integrity drift still returns an integrity error.
- What was not tested: live multi-hour systemd gateway crash-loop on a production host; real registry npm against `@openclaw/codex@beta` outside the Vitest mock harness.

target.title: fix(google): reject malformed provider media base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google provider responses could include malformed inline audio or video base64 that Node would decode permissively instead of rejecting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google music, speech, and video generation now share a strict base64 decoder before materializing provider-returned media. Inline video bytes also reuse the existing generated-video byte cap before decode so oversized payloads fail before allocating the full buffer.

## User Impact

Users get a clear provider error for malformed Google media responses, and operators keep the existing video media cap behavior without permissive base64 decoding.

## Evidence

The focused tests drive the real exported provider entrypoints — `buildGoogleSpeechProvider().synthesize()`, `buildGoogleMusicGenerationProvider().generateMusic()`, and `buildGoogleVideoGenerationProvider().generateVideo()` — with crafted valid, malformed, and oversized provider responses; the `decodeGoogleProviderBase64` guard runs as real production code on that response path (the only seam is the HTTP transport that supplies the response bytes):

- **Valid path preserved:** legitimate audio/video still materializes; the video byte cap reuses the existing generated-video limit rather than a new arbitrary value, so valid traffic is not truncated.
- **Malformed rejected:** music, speech, and video malformed inline base64 each raise a provider-specific error instead of decoding corrupt bytes.
- **Oversized rejected before buffering:** inline video bytes, direct URI downloads, and SDK file-handle downloads exceeding the media cap fail before unbounded allocation.

## Summary

**Problem**: When an Anthropic OAuth credential is inside the 5-minute refresh margin window, the auth manager correctly decides a refresh is needed and takes the global refresh lock. But `getOAuthApiKey` uses an unmargined `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check, so it silently returns the same unchanged credential without calling the provider token endpoint. **Root cause**: Two inconsistent expiry checks — the manager uses `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` (5 min) but `getOAuthApiKey` uses a bare `>=` without margin.

**Solution**: Import `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS` from `credential-state.js` and apply it in the `getOAuthApiKey` expiry check, aligning both code paths.

target.title: feat(tui): opt-in persistence and agent visibility for `!`/`!!` local shell commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

TUI-local `!`-prefixed shell commands render a live local echo but are never persisted: closing the TUI loses them, session resume never shows them, and the agent cannot see what the operator ran or what it printed — even though the `BashExecutionMessage`/`excludeFromContext` data model and the LLM-context filtering for it already exist in `packages/agent-core` (previously unused by any production code path).

Split out of #103147 per review feedback there; that PR now carries only the rendering fixes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators often run a `!` command specifically to show the agent something (Claude Code's own `!` behaves this way). But local shell output can also be sensitive, so persistence and model visibility must be a deliberate choice, not a silent default:

- The session consent prompt now offers **No** / **Yes, local only** / **Yes, and share with the agent**. **Local only is the shipped, pre-existing behavior and stays the default expectation** — nothing is saved or shared unless the operator explicitly picks the share option.
- With sharing enabled, `!cmd` persists agent-visible (the agent sees it on its next turn) and `!!cmd` persists history-only (`excludeFromContext: true`, never reaches the model). Both semantics are stated in the consent prompt itself.

Implementation: an additive, hidden (`advertise: false`, `operator.admin`) `chat.injectBashExecution` gateway RPC modeled on `chat.inject`, implemented in both TUI backends (embedded calls the shared core directly in-process; gateway goes over the RPC). No live broadcast: the originating client already rendered its own local echo. History replay renders `bashExecution` entries on session resume.

Two defects found during review/testing are fixed here as well:

- A failed spawn emits both `error` and `close`; a shared settled-guard ensures one command persists at most once.
- Rows injected while an agent run is in flight now carry `appendMode: "side"` (like `chat.inject`'s assistant bookkeeping rows) so they do not steal the run's active leaf. Without this, persisting a `!` result mid-run tripped the embedded runner's session-file fence ("session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released") and killed the run. The run adopts side entries into the chain on its next append, so the agent still sees them next turn.

## User Impact

- Default behavior is unchanged: `!` commands stay local-only unless the operator opts into sharing at the consent prompt.
- With sharing enabled, `!` output survives session resume and is visible to the agent next turn; `!!` output survives resume but never reaches the model.
- Running a shared `!` command while the agent is mid-turn no longer kills the run with a session takeover error.

## Evidence

- `src/tui/tui-local-shell.test.ts` — 12 tests: consent options (local-only default persists nothing; share option persists), `!` vs `!!` `excludeFromContext` round-trip, no-scope/no-backend skips, persistence-failure surfacing, once-only persistence on error-then-close, plus the pre-existing output-cap/UTF-16/cwd guards.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.inject-bash-execution.test.ts` — parentId chain preserved, `excludeFromContext` round-trip, **mid-run side-append regression test** (fence takeover repro), idle active-append, unresolved-identity failure.
- `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`, `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts` — both backend implementations (RPC params/result shapes; embedded in-process delegation and failure surfacing).
- `src/gateway/server-methods-list.test.ts` — hidden method not advertised, handler dispatchable.

## What Problem This Solves
Plugins have no typed, policy-enforced API for emitting AI safety events. Without it, third-party detectors (prompt injection scanners, source-trust validators) cannot contribute to the taxonomy in a safe, auditable way.

## Evidence
- `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.ts` (new) — `emitPluginSafetyEvent()` with trust-gated manifest policy
- External plugins must declare permitted event types in `safetyEventTypes` manifest field; undeclared types rejected at runtime
- `OpenClawPluginServiceContext.emitSafetyEvent` added to plugin service context
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.ts` updated as reference implementation (emits `ai_safety.external_content.consumed` on navigate)
- 16 unit tests in `src/plugins/safety-event-emission.test.ts` covering trusted/untrusted paths and manifest enforcement
- Depends on: #107176

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Emission-path fix:** with #107176 now excluding AI safety events from the untrusted `emitDiagnosticEvent()` API, manifest-authorized external plugins would have had their events silently dropped. `emitPluginSafetyEvent` now routes the authorized external path through a new core-internal `emitAuthorizedAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` (not exported from the plugin SDK), which bypasses the anti-spoofing gate only after manifest `safetyEventTypes` validation and keeps `metadata.trusted=false` so exporters (#107184) record accurate emitter provenance.

target.title: fix(line): use precise control-command check for group mention bypass
target.body:
Closes #107225

## What Problem This Solves

In a LINE group with `requireMention: true` (the default), an allowlisted member's ordinary message that just happens to contain an inline slash/bang token — `cd /home`, `go to /settings`, `!nice` — bypasses the mention requirement and gets dispatched to the agent, even though nobody @mentioned the bot. The bot pipes up on plain chatter. Only a real control command (or an actual @mention) should bypass `requireMention`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The group mention-bypass in `src/channels/mention-gating.ts` gates on `command.hasControlCommand`. LINE fed that field the broad `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` detector, whose `hasInlineCommandTokens` returns true for any `(?:^|\s)[/!][a-z]` token. That detector's job is deciding whether to *compute* CommandAuthorized metadata — per its own comment, it "errs on the side of false positives … not normal chat replies" — not whether a message *is* a control command. Using it for the bypass lets normal chat replies through the gate.

The fix routes the group path through the precise `hasControlCommand` (message starts with a configured command alias) and keeps the broad detector for DMs, which have no mention gate. This mirrors `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-access.ts`, which already uses `hasControlCommand` for the group activation path and reserves `shouldComputeCommandAuthorized` for DMs.

The group/DM split is a small `resolveLineControlCommand` helper in `group-policy.ts`, next to `resolveLineGroupRequireMention` (the file's other gating resolver); `bot-handlers.ts` (a size-capped file) calls it and stays within its line cap.

## User Impact

LINE groups with requireMention no longer surface the bot for plain messages that merely contain a `/word` or `!word` token. Real control commands from authorized members still bypass requireMention, @mentions still work, and DM behavior is unchanged. No privilege change — command execution was, and still is, gated by CommandAuthorized.

## Evidence

All checks run locally on the branch head. No LINE API involved (this is inbound gating logic).

### Red↔green — the fix's own test

Reverting **only** the group/DM split (the helper falls back to the broad detector) makes the new guard test fail, because the plain `cd /home` message now reaches the agent:

```
 × does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 FAIL  extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts > handleLineWebhookEvents > does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
      Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
```

With the fix applied, the guard passes and its companion stays green — a real `!status` from an allowlisted member still bypasses `requireMention`, so the fix narrows over-activation without breaking legitimate command bypass:

```
 ✓ does not bypass requireMention for a plain allowlisted message with an inline slash token
 ✓ still bypasses requireMention for an allowlisted real control command
```

### Behavior (group `requireMention: true`, sender in `groupAllowFrom`, no @mention)

| message | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `cd /home` (plain, inline "/" token) | `processMessage` called — dispatched to agent ❌ | skipped ✓ |
| `!status` (real control command) | dispatched ✓ | dispatched ✓ |

### Full `bot-handlers.test.ts` suite (vitest, verbose)


target.title: fix(agent): duplicate same-session turn when the gateway connection drops after accepting a run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw agent` users (the default gateway path, not `--local`) could have a single message executed twice in the **same session** when the CLI↔gateway WebSocket dropped at the wrong moment.

Once the gateway accepts a run it detaches and keeps running it independently of the CLI connection. If that connection then closes **non-transiently** before the final frame arrives — a reverse-proxy/load-balancer idle timeout, a `1006` abnormal close from a network partition, a `1012` service-restart, or any close other than a clean `1000` — the CLI fell back to an embedded run that **reused the original session**. The embedded run re-executed the same message on the very session the still-running detached gateway run already owned, producing duplicate transcript turns on one session (the `impact:session-state` symptom).

This is an edge case: the most common gateway-loss modes do not trigger it (killing the gateway also kills its in-process run; a clean `1000` close is retried as transient). It is most likely on remote gateway deployments behind a proxy/load balancer, on long-running turns, where the connection can drop between acceptance and the final frame.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause was that the "run was accepted" signal never left `agentViaGatewayCommand`: `acceptedGatewayRun` was a function-local flag, so the fallback decision in `agentCliCommand` could not tell an accepted-then-disconnected close apart from a never-accepted one, and always reused the original session.

This change propagates that signal with a dedicated `GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError` (raised only when an accepted run is hit by a non-transient close) and routes it to a **fresh** `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session — mirroring the existing gateway-timeout fallback, which already uses a fresh session precisely to avoid colliding with a still-running gateway run. The two fresh-session paths now share one helper. Cases that were already correct are unchanged: a never-accepted close still falls back on the original session (the gateway never ran it), transient `1000` closes still reconnect (the gateway's server-side dedupe returns `in_flight`), and timeouts keep their own fresh-session path.

Intentional tradeoff / non-goal: this eliminates the same-session collision and the duplicate transcript turns. It does **not** stop the already-detached gateway run from finishing, so the gateway run and the fresh embedded run each execute the turn once (two model calls, tool side effects on both, and under `--deliver` a possible second delivery on the unrelated fallback session). This is the same accepted boundary as the pre-existing gateway-timeout fallback path; fully suppressing the second run would mean an `in_flight`, no-local-result behavior change, which is out of scope here.

## User Impact

`openclaw agent` users no longer get duplicate turns written into their real session when the gateway connection drops after a run was accepted. The local fallback now runs on an isolated `gateway-fallback-<uuid>` session, so the original session's transcript stays clean and the in-flight gateway run's `runId`/`idempotencyKey` is never reused locally. Operators see a clear stderr line — `EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded agent with fresh session …` — identifying this path. No config, CLI flags, or public signatures change.

## Evidence

Provenance: static source-code analysis of the control flow (the CLI fallback decision, the transient-retry and SIGINT/SIGTERM-abort middle layers, and the gateway's server-side accepted/`in_flight` dedupe contract), plus focused regression tests.

New/updated tests in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts`:
- **New** — accepted then non-transient close → embedded fallback runs on a fresh `gateway-fallback-*` session; asserts the original `agent:main:incident-42` session is **not** reused and `fallbackReason: "gateway_connection_lost"`.
- **New** — accepted then transient `1000` close → reconnects and hits server-side dedupe `in_flight`; the embedded agent is **not** invoked (pins the intentional exclusion of transient closes; a mutation check confirmed this test fails if the transient guard is removed).
- **Preserved** — never-accepted close still reuses the explicit session key.

Local validation:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` → **70 passed**
- core typecheck `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` → exit 0
- test typecheck `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` → exit 0
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files → exit 0


### Live behavior proof — real gateway + controlled WebSocket close

In addition to the tests/static analysis above, the fix was reproduced at runtime against a real gateway.

Setup: an isolated `openclaw gateway run --dev --auth token` instance (default agent `dev`), with a transparent TCP proxy spliced between `openclaw agent` and the gateway. When the proxy observes the gateway's server→client `"status":"accepted"` frame, it forwards that frame and then half-closes the **client** socket (FIN, no WebSocket close frame). The CLI's ws client therefore reports a **1006 abnormal closure** — a non-transient `GatewayTransportError{kind:"closed"}`, the same class as a proxy/LB idle-timeout or network partition. The gateway process is left untouched, so its accepted-and-detached run keeps running independently. The CLI is pointed at the proxy via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` and runs the gateway path (no `--local`).

The two runs below are identical except for the code under test (without vs. with this PR), same isolated gateway, same agent, same proxy:

```text
proxy (both runs): MATCH "status":"accepted" … sessionKey=agent:dev:main → forward → FIN → CLI sees 1006

BEFORE (without this PR) — the bug:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway agent failed; running embedded agent:
    GatewayTransportError: gateway closed (1006 abnormal closure (no close frame)): no close reason
  embedded run: runId=7095f9a4-…-ac4d06fe2083   lane=session:agent:dev:main
  → the generic fallback REUSES the original session agent:dev:main and reuses the
    in-flight gateway runId → duplicate turn collides with the still-running gateway run.

AFTER (with this PR) — fixed:
  EMBEDDED FALLBACK: Gateway connection closed after the run was accepted; running embedded
    agent with fresh session gateway-fallback-0530ad46-… to avoid duplicating the in-flight
    gateway run 3cff5b23-…709e60fd on agent:dev:main: GatewayAgentAcceptedRunDisconnectError
  embedded run: runId=sessionId=gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
                lane=session:agent:dev:explicit:gateway-fallback-0530ad46-…
  → the accepted-disconnect path routes to a FRESH gateway-fallback-* session; the original
    agent:dev:main session is never re-executed locally.
```

Note: the isolated instance has no model key, so a `401 Unauthorized` follows in both runs — but only *after* the decisive routing line, and symmetrically in both — so it does not affect the comparison. This proves the session-routing change (which session the embedded fallback adopts after an accepted-then-disconnected close), which is the substance of the bug, rather than two completed model turns.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returns, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a property assignment backfill at the return site in `createWithAdapter`: if `result.provider` exists but `result.provider.model` is falsy, assign the resolved model. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed for new indexes; existing dirty indexes require a one-time `openclaw memory status --index`.

## Evidence

### Code Evidence

`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts:245-247`:
```ts
if (result.provider && !result.provider.model) {
  result.provider.model = createOptions.model;
}
```

Direct property assignment (not spread operator) so prototype methods on the provider object are preserved. Regression test at `embeddings.test.ts:350-370`.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `provider.model` is empty when the adapter returns no model, causing identity mis-match and persistent dirty index.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/provider-model-backfill-90042-reborn`, commit 03f60bc022.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm openclaw memory status --deep
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
Memory Search (main)
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Sources: memory
Indexed: 50/131 files · 697 chunks
Dirty: yes
Store: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
Embeddings: ready
Index identity: index was built for model fts-only, expected Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt
Fix: Run: openclaw memory status --index --agent main
```

Key observations:
1. **`Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B`** — The backfill works. `provider.model` carries the resolved model name, not `""`.
2. **`expected Qwen3-Embedding-8B`** — The identity check at `manager-reindex-state.ts:145` now receives a proper model.
3. **`index was built for model fts-only`** — This is the *existing dirty index* created before this patch, proving the bug existed.
4. The identity flow (`this.provider.model` → `resolveMemoryIndexIdentityState` → `expectedModel`) executes the same code path as every restart. With this PR, fresh indexes will store the correct model and remain clean.

**Observed result after fix**: After a one-time reindex, the new `meta.model` will match `expectedModel` and the index is clean. Without this fix, `expectedModel` stays `fts-only` and the index stays dirty forever.

**What was not tested**: Full reindex (`openclaw memory status --index`) on this workspace — blocked by a local `sqlite-vec` native extension load issue unrelated to the PR logic. The identity validation code path (`resolveMemoryIndexIdentityState`) is proven correct by the `expected Qwen3-Embedding-8B` output above, which is the exact function called on every gateway restart.

## Regression Test Plan

| Test file | What it covers | Why minimal |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts` | 3 scenarios: explicit model preserves value, empty model backfills, provider with correct model unchanged | Direct coverage of the changed function |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/generic-embedding-provider.bridge.test.ts` | `createEmbeddingProvider` + identity round-trip | Covers the call site in the bridge path |

Supersedes #91660 (31 days old, merge conflicts, larger diff with unrelated deletions). This branch is based on latest upstream/main with a focused +5/-2 diff.

target.title: fix(ui): prevent CLS on chat images with min-height placeholder
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Chat messages containing images cause **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)** during image loading. The original CSS used `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` as a placeholder — but the image can still grow from 40px to the rule's 200px `max-height`, pushing every message below it downward by up to **160 px**. On slow connections this means content the user is actively reading jumps mid-sentence. Seven of the ten image-extraction paths in `extractImages()` (OpenAI `image_url`, Anthropic `input_image`, `openclaw_pairing_qr`, and transcript media) do not attach `width`/`height` to the `ImageBlock`, so the rendered `` tag has no intrinsic dimensions. The browser collapses the element to its minimum placeholder size — previously 40×40 — then reflows the page once the image bytes arrive. ## Why This Change Was Made Replace `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` with `aspect-ratio: 3 / 2`. This reserves a box whose **height is proportional to its width**, matching the `max-width` / `max-height` constraint (300 / 200 = 3:2). For the `` elements that already carry `width`/`height` HTML attributes (3 of 10 extraction paths), the intrinsic aspect ratio takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` — these images are unaffected. For the remaining 7 paths that provide no dimensions, the browser now computes a default size from the `aspect-ratio` + `max-width` + `max-height` constraint tuple. When the actual image loads at its natural aspect ratio, `object-fit: contain` ensures it fits within the already-reserved box. The residual CLS is only the difference between the 3:2 placeholder ratio and the image's actual ratio (bounded by `object-fit`), rather than a hard 40–200 px gap. ## User Impact Messages below images stay anchored in place during image loading. Image placeholders are sized to match the image's final display area, not an arbitrary 40 px minimum. The muted background (`var(--bg-muted)`) remains as a visual loading indicator. ## Evidence ### CLS measurement — BEFORE (min-height: 40px) vs AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3/2) A proof harness renders two identical images (300×200, 3:2) without `width`/`height` attributes inside a 300 px-wide flex container matching the chat layout. The reference element below each image is measured before and after the image finishes loading. ``` Image: 300×200 (3:2 aspect ratio, matches max-width / max-height constraint) Container: flex, 400px wide (matches chat bubble) BEFORE (min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px): Pre-load image height: 40px (min-height constraint) Post-load image height: 200px (max-height, object-fit: contain) CLS downstream shift: 160px ← content jumps 160px AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3 / 2): Pre-load image height: ~200px (300px × 2/3, capped by max-height) Post-load image height: 200px (intrinsic 300×200 fits the reserved box) CLS downstream shift: ~0px ← placeholder matches final size ``` **Proof harness**: `node:http` server at `localhost:18765` serving the real CSS rules and a delayed-response PNG (1s artificial latency). DOM `getBoundingClientRect().top` measurements for the reference element confirm the 160 px shift in the `min-height` case and ~0 px shift in the `aspect-ratio` case. ### Build proof ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s ``` Compiled CSS audit confirms `aspect-ratio:3/2` is present and `min-height`/`min-width` are absent: ``` $ grep -oP 'chat-message-image\{[^}]*\}' dist/control-ui/assets/*.css border-radius:var(--radius-md);object-fit:contain;aspect-ratio:3/2; background:var(--bg-muted);max-width:300px;max-height:200px; transition:transform .15s ease-out ``` ### Browser behavior proof (aspect-ratio precedence) Per the CSS Sizing specification, a replaced element's **intrinsic aspect ratio** (from `width`/`height` HTML attributes) takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. Images from the 3 extraction paths that do carry dimensions are unaffected. The CSS `aspect-ratio` only applies to the 7 paths where the `` tag has no `width`/`height` attributes. ### Negative control (previous 40px fix) The `min-height: 40px` approach guarantees a downstream shift of up to `max-height - 40px`. For the 300×200 constraint, that is a worst-case 160 px CLS — the regressed behavior is trivially measurable by DOM inspection: any image with a natural height above 40 px will cause the reference line to move. ## Regression Test Plan ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s $ git diff --stat HEAD~1..HEAD ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css | 12 +++++++++--- 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-) ``` No runtime logic changed. The CSS addition only affects the computed dimensions of `` elements with class `.chat-message-image` that lack `width`/`height` HTML attributes. ## Root Cause `.chat-message-image` (`ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:781`) had `max-width: 300px` and `max-height: 200px` without any aspect-ratio information. The previous fix (#107108) added `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px`, which gives the browser a nonzero minimum but does **not** constrain the element's height proportionally to its final rendered area. An image that renders at 200 px tall still shifts from 40 px → 200 px. The browser's box-sizing algorithm needs either intrinsic dimensions (from HTML `width`/`height`) or a CSS `aspect-ratio` to compute proportional height before the image bytes arrive. Without proportional sizing, the placeholder height is always an underestimate, and the resulting CLS scales with the gap between the minimum and the actual rendered height. Seven of the ten `extractImages()` paths never provide `width`/`height` fields on the `ImageBlock`, so the HTML `` tags for those paths have no `width`/`height` attributes. The CSS `aspect-ratio` property is the correct universal fallback — it gives the browser a proportional size for every image, regardless of source format, and defers to intrinsic dimensions when they are present. ## AI Assistance Analysis, CSS fix, proof harness, and PR body drafted with agent assistance. All build commands were run locally.

target.title: feat(line): wire base.allowlist config-edit adapter
target.body:
Closes #106637

## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw allow line <id>` — or the in-chat `/allowlist add|remove` command — against the LINE channel replies `⚠️ line does not support dm allowlist edits via /allowlist.` instead of editing the allowlist. A LINE operator can't add or remove a DM/group allowlisted user at runtime; they have to stop and hand-edit the config file, even though the `channels.line.allowFrom` / `channels.line.groupAllowFrom` fields already exist. LINE is the only DM/group channel with this gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core `/allowlist` handler refuses whenever a channel plugin has no `allowlist.applyConfigEdit` (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.ts:465`). Every other DM/group channel declares one: Telegram, Signal, iMessage and WhatsApp via `buildDmGroupAccountAllowlistAdapter`; Discord and Slack via the legacy variant. LINE's `createChatChannelPlugin({ base })` never wired it.

This PR wires `buildDmGroupAccountAllowlistAdapter` into LINE's `base`, matching the Telegram/Signal shape exactly — no hand-rolled logic:

- **DM + group + `all` scopes.** LINE stores both `allowFrom` and `groupAllowFrom`, so the non-legacy DM/group builder is correct (not the legacy DM-only variant Discord/Slack use).
- **Per-group overrides** via `createFlatAllowlistOverrideResolver` over `groups.*.allowFrom` — LINE group config is flat (no Telegram-style nested topics), so the flat resolver is the right one.
- **LINE-specific entry normalization** (stripping the `line:` / `line:user:` prefix) reuses the existing `lineConfigAdapter.formatAllowFrom`, so a `line:user:U…` entry and the bare `U…` resolve to the same list member.

No config schema change (the fields already exist) and no dependency/lockfile changes.

## User Impact

`/allowlist add dm <lineUserId>`, `/allowlist remove …`, and the `group` scope now edit `channels.line.allowFrom` / `channels.line.groupAllowFrom` at the correct account scope — same UX as every other channel. Behavior is unchanged for other channels and for LINE users who never issue the command.

## Evidence

All local — this is a config-edit surface, no LINE API involved.

**Before vs after — actual `linePlugin.allowlist` output, identical inputs:**

BEFORE (unwired — current `main`):
```json
{ "wired": false, "configAfterDmAdd": {}, "configAfterGroupAdd": {} }
```

AFTER (this PR):
```json
{
  "wired": true,
  "addDmResult": {
    "kind": "ok", "changed": true, "pathLabel": "channels.line.allowFrom",
    "writeTarget": { "kind": "channel", "scope": { "channelId": "line" } }
  },
  "configAfterDmAdd":    { "channels": { "line": { "allowFrom":      ["Uc0ffeecafe00000000000000deadbeef"] } } },
  "configAfterGroupAdd": { "channels": { "line": { "groupAllowFrom": ["Ubeefbeefbeef00000000000000c0ffee"] } } },
  "readConfig": {
    "dmAllowFrom":    ["Uc0ffeecafe00000000000000deadbeef"],
    "groupAllowFrom": ["Ubeefbeefbeef00000000000000c0ffee"],
    "dmPolicy": "allowlist", "groupPolicy": "allowlist",
    "groupOverrides": [ { "label": "Cabc123", "entries": ["Udeadbeef0000000000000000cafe0000"] } ]
  }
}
```

**New contract test** — `extensions/line/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts`:
```
✓ exposes the config-edit contract
✓ supports the 'dm' / 'group' / 'all' scope
✓ reads dm/group allowlists and group overrides from line config
✓ adds a dm allowlist entry under channels.line.allowFrom
✓ adds a group allowlist entry under channels.line.groupAllowFrom
✓ treats a line:-prefixed entry as already present via the line normalizer
✓ removes a dm allowlist entry and keeps the rest

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Red↔green** — removing only the `allowlist:` wiring turns all 9 red; restoring makes them green:
```
Tests  9 failed (9)   ← wiring removed
Tests  9 passed (9)   ← wiring restored
```

**Static checks** — tsgo extensions (prod + test): pass · `pnpm lint:extensions` (oxlint): pass · `oxfmt --check` on touched files: pass.

target.title: fix(deepinfra): use OpenAI video end point and tag DeepSeek thinking format
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Two user-visible DeepInfra integration problems: **Video generation.** Fixes an issue where generating video through the DeepInfra provider used DeepInfra's legacy native inference path and a small, hardcoded set of video models. Newly released DeepInfra video models (Veo 3.1, Wan 2.x, Pixverse, Seedance, …) never appeared, and the video surface didn't behave like OpenClaw's other DeepInfra modalities (chat, image, speech), which already run over DeepInfra's OpenAI-compatible API. DeepInfra has since shipped an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/openai/videos` endpoint and tagged its video models, so the catalog can be discovered live. **DeepSeek replies.** Fixes an issue where chatting with a DeepInfra DeepSeek model (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash) leaked the model's raw reasoning/tool-call markup — `<|DSML|…>` and `reasoning_content` — into the visible reply, and could drop tool calls. Because DeepInfra serves every model family over a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, OpenClaw treated DeepSeek as a generic "openai" model and never recovered its DeepSeek-dialect output. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Video** now targets DeepInfra's async `/v1/openai/videos` job endpoint (submit → poll → result URL), matching the other OpenAI-compatible surfaces, and builds its model list from live discovery filtered by the `video-gen` tag, with a small static fallback when no API key is configured. Scope: text-to-video only (image/video reference inputs remain unsupported). - **DeepSeek** is declared with `thinkingFormat: "deepseek"` for the `deepseek-ai/*` family (the same per-family dialect approach already used for Qwen), so core strips/recovers DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` and DSML tool calls instead of passing them through; models carrying the `reasoning` / `reasoning_effort` tag are marked reasoning-capable so thinking levels apply. ## User Impact - **Video:** Users get the current DeepInfra text-to-video catalog, auto-discovered (no more stale hardcoded list), generated through the same OpenAI-compatible flow as the other modalities. No config or workflow change needed. - **DeepSeek:** DeepSeek models on DeepInfra now return clean replies — no leaked `<|DSML|…>` / reasoning markup — tool calls work reliably, and reasoning / "thinking" levels are honored. ## Evidence Verified live on a hosted OpenClaw instance running this branch (DeepInfra provider; agent model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), driven via `openclaw agent`, with outbound HTTP captured at the network layer. **1 — Video uses the new endpoint + tag discovery.** Captured request timeline across two generations: - `GET /v1/openai/models?sort_by=openclaw&filter=with_meta` → 200 — tag discovery (returns 13 `video-gen` models: Veo 3.1/-fast, Wan 2.6/2.2-T2V, Pixverse-6 / T2V / T2V-HD, Seedance 2.0 / 1.5-Pro, Cosmos3, LTX2, p-video) - `POST /v1/openai/videos` → 200 — async submit (returns a `videos_` job) - `GET /v1/openai/videos/videos_` → 200, polled ~every 5 s until succeeded - **zero `/v1/inference` calls**; - MP4s rendered and attached to the reply. _📸 Screenshot: `capture_events` timeline (POST /v1/openai/videos + polls)_ https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bc82632-378f-4f90-bf4d-f84ac915ff40 **2 — DeepSeek thinking format.** - `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` discovery tags: `["chat","prompt_cache","reasoning"]` - `openclaw agent --thinking high` on a reasoning prompt → correct step-by-step answer with **no `<|DSML|…>` / `reasoning_content` in the reply**, even though the DeepInfra response body did contain a `reasoning_content` field (confirmed in the capture) — i.e. it's recovered, not leaked. _📸 Screenshot: clean DeepSeek reasoning reply_ [request.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29214104/request.json) Focused provider tests cover the video submit→poll→result flow (success, immediate-success, job failure, malformed payloads) and the DeepSeek-family tagging.

target.title: fix(memory-core): preserve canonical cache rows during legacy migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading to v2026.7.1 can get stuck in a Gateway startup loop when a legacy Memory Core sidecar and the canonical database contain the same embedding-cache identity with different derived payloads. `doctor --fix` reports a migration conflict and leaves the sidecar in place; Gateway preflight treats that warning as fatal, so every restart repeats the failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The legacy migration already uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` with `(provider, model, provider_key, hash)` as the cache identity. This change accepts a collision when that identity, its declared dimensions, and its actual embedding length match, retaining the canonical derived embedding and timestamp. A dimension or embedding-length mismatch still fails the import, rolls back the savepoint, and preserves the legacy sidecar for a safe retry.

## User Impact

Affected Gateways can complete startup without deleting either database. Legacy sources, chunks, and non-colliding cache rows still migrate; compatible canonical cache rows win; dimensionally incompatible collisions remain protected instead of being archived.

## Evidence

- Before, a disposable Blaxel reproduction emitted the `embedding_cache` migration warning, retained the legacy sidecar, and refused Gateway startup on repeated starts.
- After, the legacy cache row migrated, the compatible canonical collision was retained, the sidecar was archived, a second migration was a no-op, and Gateway reached ready.
- Regression coverage proves declared-dimension mismatch, same-`dims`/different actual length, and malformed canonical JSON each warn, roll back, and leave the sidecar unarchived.

Blaxel sandbox `openclaw-271-migration-repro` (Linux x86_64, OpenClaw 2026.7.1 state fixture, with this PR's predicate applied to the compiled doctor module):

```text
BEFORE
Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import ... embedding_cache rows conflict ...
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.

AFTER — compatible collision
DOCTOR_EXIT=0
Migrated Memory Core legacy memory index ... (0 source(s), 0 chunk(s), 1 cache row(s))
Archived Memory Core legacy memory index sidecar -> .../memory/main.sqlite.migrated
canonical={embedding:"[9,9,9]",dims:3,updated_at:99}
legacySidecarExists=false archivedSidecarExists=true
SECOND_DOCTOR_EXIT=0 SECOND_DOCTOR_MEMORY_MIGRATIONS=0
[gateway] http server listening (8 plugins ...; 1.1s)
[gateway] ready

AFTER — same dims, incompatible actual length
canonical={embedding:"[9,9,9,9]",dims:3}; legacy={embedding:"[1,0,0]",dims:3}
Skipped Memory Core legacy memory index import ... embedding_cache rows conflict ...
LEGACY_SIDECAR_PRESERVED=1 ARCHIVE_CREATED=0
```

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-core/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 32/32 passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/memory-core/doctor-contract-api.ts extensions/memory-core/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — passed

target.title: fix(oauth): make getOAuthApiKey refresh within the standard margin (issue #103846)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getOAuthApiKey` in `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts` decided whether to refresh an OAuth token using a raw expiry check (`Date.now() >= creds.expires`). The OAuth manager gate, `hasUsableOAuthCredential` (`src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts`), decides refresh using a 5-minute margin (`DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`).

When a credential was inside the margin window but not yet past its raw expiry, the manager correctly decided a refresh was needed, took the global refresh lock, and delegated to `getOAuthApiKey` — but `getOAuthApiKey` saw `now < expires` and **skipped the refresh silently**, returning the unchanged credential as if the refresh succeeded. The caller then used a stale token until raw expiry, instead of refreshing early.

## Evidence

- `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts:105` used `if (Date.now() >= creds.expires)` (raw expiry).
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/credential-state.ts:54` `hasUsableOAuthCredential` uses `resolveTokenExpiryState(..., { expiringWithinMs: refreshMarginMs })` with `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000`.
- Callers `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts:213` and `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts:466` are refresh paths that expect margin-aware refresh; neither relied on the old raw-expiry skip.
- New regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` covers the margin window (4 min remaining → refresh fires), comfortably-outside (30 min → no refresh), and past-expiry (→ refresh fires).

## Fix

Replaced the raw `Date.now() >= creds.expires` check with the shared `hasUsableOAuthCredential(creds)`, so the low-level delegate uses the same margin as the manager gate. One import, one condition. No behavior change for the two existing callers other than the intended early-refresh.

## Runtime Proof

`scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs` mirrors the exact decision functions from `credential-state.ts` (`resolveTokenExpiryState`, `hasUsableOAuthCredential`) and the old/new `getOAuthApiKey` gates, then runs a credential 2 minutes from expiry (inside the 5-minute margin):

```text
$ node scripts/proof-oauth-margin.mjs
MARGIN_MS=300000
creds.expires - now = 120000 ms (inside margin)
hasUsableOAuthCredential = false (manager gate: REFRESH)
OLD getOAuthApiKey refresh? false  -> returns unchanged creds (STALE TOKEN)
NEW getOAuthApiKey refresh? true  -> refreshes within margin (FRESH TOKEN)

RESULT: PASS — within margin, OLD skipped refresh (bug) but NEW refreshes (fixed)
```

The same margin window is covered by the committed regression test `src/llm/utils/oauth/index.test.ts` (no real Anthropic credentials needed).

Closes #103846

target.title: fix(google): anchor model-ID regexes to prevent false-positive substring matches
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Model-ID matching in `google-shared.ts` uses substring patterns that match false positives on hypenated lookalikes (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash` matches `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`).

**Solution**: Replace loose `\b` word-boundary suffixes with `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead — an explicit model-ID contract that only allows end-of-string or non-identifier continuation (e.g. `@`, spaces). All 6 model-ID regexes and `String.includes()` calls are now properly anchored.

## Changes

| Regex | Before | After |
|------|------|------|
| isGemma4Model | `/gemma-?4/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemma-?4(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3ProModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3FlashModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-pro budget | `.includes("2.5-pro")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash-lite budget | `.includes("2.5-flash-lite")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash-lite(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash budget | `.includes("2.5-flash")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |

The `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead prevents matching when followed by model-name continuation characters:
- `gemini-2.5-flash` does NOT match `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` (hyphen suffix rejected)
- `gemini-2.5-flash` DOES match `gemini-2.5-flash@preview` (allowed suffix)

/cc @openclaw/clawsweeper

target.title: [codex] active-memory default to configured agents
target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:
  OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a Linux host with a systemd user gateway, Telegram group topics routed to `main`, `sementes`, `cloudfarm`, and `pedro-agenda`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  Applied the equivalent runtime change locally, removed `active-memory.config.agents`, restarted `openclaw-gateway`, then checked gateway status and memory search.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
openclaw gateway status --deep
Gateway version: 2026.6.5
Runtime: running
Capability: admin-capable
```

```text
journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway --since "3 minutes ago"
[gateway] http server listening (12 plugins: active-memory, brave, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair, file-transfer, memory-core, openai, phone-control, talk-voice, telegram; 12.1s)
```

```text
openclaw memory search --query "Pedro SeedSearch Markus" --max-results 5
0.545 memory/pendencias-grupo.md:1-21
0.516 memory/2026-03-31.md:1-37
0.453 memory/dreaming/light/2026-06-05.md:43-72
```

- Observed result after fix:
  Active Memory no longer required a hardcoded `config.agents` list to apply across configured agents.
- What was not tested:
  A fresh live Telegram command round-trip was not captured on the final PR branch.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints:
  The production server was restored to upstream behavior after proof collection, using an explicit `config.agents` list until this PR is merged upstream.
- Before evidence:
  Reading the prior plugin implementation showed `normalizePluginConfig({}).agents` became `[]`, while `isEnabledForAgent` requires `config.agents.includes(agentId)`.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
pnpm docs:list
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts
node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/concepts/active-memory.md
node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check
node --import tsx -e "import { testing } from './extensions/active-memory/index.ts'; const cfg={agents:{list:[{id:'main'},{id:'support'}]}}; console.log(JSON.stringify({ omitted: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}, cfg).agents, empty: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents: []}, cfg).agents, explicit: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents:['support']}, cfg).agents, implicitMain: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}).agents }, null, 2));"
git diff --check upstream/main -- docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

Regression coverage added:

- `defaults to all configured agents when no active-memory agent allowlist is set`
- `preserves an empty active-memory agent allowlist`
- `defaults to the implicit main agent when no agent list is configured`
- `keeps an explicit active-memory agent allowlist`

CI after the latest push:

- Pending for commit `b7e75ed8eaa7`. Prior CI was green on `fdf408d1e55464aced878f0fee85201324590de3`.

Final-head normalization proof on `b7e75ed8eaa7`:

```json
{
  "omitted": [
    "main",
    "support"
  ],
  "empty": [],
  "explicit": [
    "support"
  ],
  "implicitMain": [
    "main"
  ]
}
```

Autoreview note:

- The final commit review still flags the omitted-`agents` default as a maintainer compatibility decision. That is the intended product change in this PR and remains called out below; the explicit empty-list finding has been addressed.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

Highest-risk area:
Operators who intentionally omitted `config.agents` expecting Active Memory to run nowhere would now get Active Memory for configured agents, or `main` in minimal configs. Explicit `config.agents: []` continues to target no agents.

Risk mitigation:
Explicit `config.agents: []` remains a no-target allowlist, and explicit non-empty `config.agents` still behaves as an allowlist. Operators can set `enabled: false`, disable the plugin entry, set `agents: []`, or provide a narrow `agents` list when they want less coverage. The docs and manifest help now state the omitted default and the explicit-empty behavior.

target.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins
target.body:
Fixes #106189

## Summary

- Classify non-E404 npm metadata precheck failures as a closed installer error (`NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`).
- Normalize npm 12 singleton-array metadata in the update-check parser, matching the already-merged install-path normalization.
- Keep a healthy installed npm plugin enabled when `openclaw update repair` cannot fetch metadata before replacement begins.
- Preserve the existing fail-closed behavior for package-not-found (E404), integrity, security, policy, and post-resolution install failures.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** A transient npm registry failure no longer turns a working plugin unavailable during core-update repair or `plugins update --all`.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106189
- Related #84256 (partial_overlap: different root cause — recorded-version reuse)
- Related #82368 (partial_overlap: Codex config migration, different root cause)
- Related #102883 (merged PR: fixed sibling install metadata parser npm 12 array handling)
- Competing #107063 (same state-preservation boundary, omits this PR's update-check parser normalization)

## Root Cause

| Problem | Introduced | Author | Intent |
|---------|-----------|--------|--------|
| `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` object-only parser | `0946e37523` (Apr 23) | steipete | Designed for npm 11 single-object output — **fixed by `96f0983a85` (Jul 11, PR #102883)** |
| `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` rejects arrays | `62fad3da86` (Jun 17) | Vincent Koc | Same-era design, missed npm 12 fix — **fixed here** |
| `disableOnFailure` with no failure classification | `7c0f5463a5` (May 4) | Vincent Koc | Isolate broken plugin packages — **fixed here** |

- **Root cause:** Non-E404 npm metadata failures had no closed error code at the resolver/installer boundary; the update lifecycle treated every metadata failure as a failed replacement and disabled an otherwise healthy plugin.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `openclaw update repair` → `updateNpmInstalledPlugins({ disableOnFailure: true })` → npm metadata precheck → update failure policy.
- **Boundary crossed:** `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` classifies the failure, `installPluginFromNpmSpec` carries the code, and the update lifecycle owns the non-destructive decision.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The decision is made at the lifecycle that owns plugin-state removal, before a replacement install begins.
- **What did NOT change:** E404 handling, integrity checks, security checks, policy checks, post-resolution install failures, multi-version array rejection.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A real `openclaw update repair` metadata request failure must not disable a healthy installed npm plugin or remove its activation state before replacement starts.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.15.0, current built OpenClaw checkout (`node scripts/build-all.mjs cliStartup`, 18.2s), exact PR head `0491cab9696c`, isolated registry `http://127.0.0.1:1`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:1 openclaw update repair --json --yes --timeout 5`

- **Evidence after fix:** The controlled CLI run produced the following state evidence.

```text
metadata request: ECONNREFUSED from http://127.0.0.1:1 (npm exit code 1, stderr empty, not E404)
plugin outcome: error; postUpdate.plugins.changed=false; postUpdate.plugins.npm.changed=false
entries.codex.enabled: unchanged (true before and after)
plugins.allow contains codex: unchanged
plugins.deny contains codex: unchanged
slots.memory: unchanged ("codex" before and after)
slots.contextEngine: unchanged ("codex" before and after)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The command reported the metadata failure (`npm view produced incomplete package metadata`, category `metadata-env` → `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`) and retained the healthy plugin's entry, activation-list membership, and slot assignments unchanged.

- **Contrast with E404 behavior:** When `npm view` stderr contains `E404`, the plugin is disabled, removed from allow/deny, and slots are reset (`changed=true`). This fail-closed E404 path remains unchanged.

- **What was not tested:** A live public npm registry or third-party provider; the failure was intentionally produced by an isolated local registry endpoint. macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android were not tested.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts` and `src/plugins/update.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A registry-timeout metadata precheck with `disableOnFailure` preserves the entry, allow/deny lists, slots, and `changed=false` while returning an error outcome.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It covers the destructive update-repair state transition and verifies the resolver category used to distinguish it.

## Scope and risk

No public config, schema, protocol, or default changes. The patch is limited to metadata-failure classification, update-check parser normalization, and update-failure policy. npm E404 and every existing post-metadata install failure remain fail-closed.

- **Related open PR scan:** #107063 implements the same non-E404 metadata-failure state-preservation boundary and supplies real CLI proof, but omits this PR's sibling update-check parser normalization. The branches are not currently interchangeable.
- **Out of scope:** No config shape, schema, protocol, default, migration, dependency, or npm parsing behavior (beyond the singleton-array update-check normalization already shipped for the install path in #102883) is changed.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility: the patch changes upgrade-repair failure policy for an entire class of metadata errors, determining whether existing plugin configuration is preserved or destructively rewritten.
- **Risk explanation:** The change alters only one closed pre-install error path in the plugin update lifecycle.
- **Why acceptable:** It preserves an existing healthy state on a transient metadata failure without treating the update as successful; destructive behavior remains for known-missing packages and all existing post-metadata failures.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix — focused canonical bug fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the Linux CLI path exercised above; no cross-platform claim is made.
- **Patch quality notes:** Five focused source/test files; no lockfile, dependency, config, documentation, or changelog changes.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts` — 19 passed
- `pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts` — 116 passed

## Competition / linked PR analysis

#107063 is the direct open competitor for the same state-preservation boundary. It supplies real CLI proof but omits the sibling update-check singleton-array parser normalization. This PR includes both the state-preservation boundary and the parser fix. Maintainers should select one canonical landing path; if #107063 is chosen, the update-check parser normalization should be tracked separately.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw plugins update --all` no longer disable healthy plugins when npm view metadata fails for any reason (format incompatibility, timeout, network error)
- `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw update repair` can recover plugins disabled by earlier npm 12 failures

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — additive change, does not affect npm 11 behavior
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `762bb4bc90`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `47d37804a8`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-small-2` failure was in `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts` for `SettingsProTabSections.swift`, outside both touched `extensions/memory-lancedb/**` files. The main-branch iOS fix is included by this rebase; fresh final-head CI is running.

target.title: fix(config): restore env changes before rethrowing INVALID_CONFIG
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadConfigLocal()` applies `env.vars` to `process.env` during config resolution via
`resolveConfigForRead()` → `applyConfigEnvVars()`. When config validation fails with
`INVALID_CONFIG`, the catch block at line 1942 rethrows without restoring the env
snapshot, leaking env side effects into the running process.

**Trigger**: `openclaw.json` with valid `env.vars` entries but other invalid config sections
(e.g. `gateway.port: "invalid"` where a number is expected).

## Why This Change Was Made

Three other code paths in the same file already follow the correct pattern of calling
`restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged()` before returning/retrying after config operations that
modify env:

| Location | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Line 1906 | `loadConfigLocal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 2169 | `readConfigFileSnapshotInternal()` — retry after suspicious recovery |
| Line 3242 | `writeAndActivateConfig()` — rollback after write failure |

The `INVALID_CONFIG` path was the only one missing this cleanup.

**Revision 9b867e8**: The original commit (801810f) declared `envBeforeRead` with `const`
inside the `try` block, making it inaccessible in the `catch` block (ReferenceError).
This revision hoists the declaration to `let` above `try`, matching JavaScript scoping
rules (`const` in `try` is not visible in `catch`).

## User Impact

- Before: invalid config with `env.vars` → env leaked → subsequent operations see wrong env values
- After: env is properly restored before rethrowing, matching the behavior of all other error/retry paths

## Evidence

### Focused Regression Tests

`src/config/io.invalid-config-env-restore.test.ts` — 5 tests, all passing:

1. `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged` unit: removes newly injected key
2. `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged` unit: restores overwritten key
3. `restoreEnvChangesIfUnchanged` unit: preserves externally modified key (TOCTOU-safe)
4. Integration: valid `env.vars` + invalid `gateway.port` → env restored on INVALID_CONFIG
5. Integration: env key with pre-existing value overwritten by config → restored on INVALID_CONFIG

```
pnpm test src/config/io.invalid-config-env-restore.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Real Behavior Proof (Live CLI)

**Scenario 1: New env key injected by config, then restored**

```bash

$ echo '{"env":{"vars":{"PROOF_LEAK_TEST_VAR":"should-not-leak"}},"gateway":{"port":"not-a-number"}}' \
  > $TMPDIR/.openclaw/openclaw.json

$ HOME=$TMPDIR pnpm openclaw status
OpenClaw config is invalid
File: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Problem:
```

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

### Negative control — without handler, process crashes (current main)

Real `child_process.spawn`, stdout pipe destroyed without an `error` handler:

```
$ node -e "
import('node:child_process').then(({spawn}) => {
  const child = spawn('sh', ['-c', 'echo hello; sleep 0.2']);
  child.stdout.on('data', () => {});
  // Deliberately NO stdout.on('error') — matching current main code
  child.stdout.destroy(new Error('EPIPE stdout broken'));
});
"
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: EPIPE stdout broken
    at [eval]:6:24
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    ...
```

→ **ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR — process crashes.** This is the exact failure mode in the sandbox exec server.

### After fix — with handler, caught gracefully (this PR)

Same real `spawn`, plus production-pattern `stdout.on("error")` + `stderr.on("error")` handlers — proof 2 destoys stdout mid-stream, proof 3 registers and verifies both handlers fire with the exact destroy pattern:

```
── Proof 2: stdout error WITH handler → caught gracefully
  [stdout] chunk #1: chunk0
  [stdout] → destroying stream: EPIPE stdout broken (simulated)
  [stdout/error] caught: EPIPE stdout broken (simulated)
  [close] exit=0 signal=null
  ✓ stdout "error" handler fired and prevented ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR

── Proof 3: production handler pattern (matching processes.ts)
  [stdout/error] production handler: EPIPE stdout broken (production pattern)
  [stderr/error] production handler (warn): EPIPE stderr broken (production pattern)
  ✓ stdout "error" listener registered (1 listener(s))
  ✓ stderr "error" listener registered (1 listener(s))

ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Before**: `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` → exec server dies
**After**: error caught → `managed.failure` recorded → `SIGTERM` → close path finalizes normally

### Observed result

- The production-pattern handler catches the stream error and prevents the crash
- stdout error records failure + signals the child (close lifecycle finalizes)
- stderr error is warning-only, does not kill an otherwise healthy process

### What was not tested

Live Codex sandbox pipe failure in a running exec-server process (requires resource-exhaustion repro).

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

```
$ oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts — exit 0
$ oxfmt --check — clean
```

- Realistic-stream tests with `PassThrough` stdout/stderr/stdin exercise the production close path, including `finalizeProcess()` → `stdin.destroy()` → `finalizeExec`.
- `finalizeExec` type now uses `NonNullable<SandboxBackendHandle["finalizeExec"]>` imported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/sandbox` — `check-test-types` passes.
- Branch rebased on upstream main (f72e936f26).

## Root Cause

In `runProcess()` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.ts`), `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` are `Readable` streams returned by `child_process.spawn`. The code subscribes to `"data"` events on both but registers no `"error"` listener. Node.js does not forward readable-stream errors to the child process `"error"` event — per the Node.js docs, an unhandled `"error"` on a stream is a fatal `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` that terminates the owning process. When a sandbox pipe breaks (e.g. EPIPE, ECONNRESET), the exec server process crashes entirely, taking down all concurrent sandbox sessions. The fix adds explicit error handlers: stdout errors record the failure and terminate the managed child via `SIGTERM` (letting the existing `"close"` handler own finalization), and stderr errors warn without disrupting execution — matching the adjacent Codex app-server client contract.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): treat U+2028/U+2029 as paragraph boundaries when chunking
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model output can contain Unicode LINE SEPARATOR (U+2028) and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (U+2029) characters. `chunkByParagraph()` normalizes `\r\n?` to `\n` for blank-line detection, but does not normalize U+2028/U+2029. When these characters appear instead of `\n\n`, the entire block stays as one fused chunk instead of splitting at paragraph boundaries — producing oversized message chunks on line-oriented channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-step normalization:

1. **U+2029 → `\n\n`** (blank line): U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR is semantically a paragraph boundary, equivalent to a blank line.
2. **U+2028 → `\n`** (single newline): U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is a single line break within a paragraph.

The two-step order ensures consecutive U+2028  also produces a blank line (`\n` + `\n\n` = `\n\n\n` — blank line detected by `\n[\t ]*\n+`).

## User Impact

Prevents oversized single-chunk messages on line-oriented channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal, iMessage, Discord) when model output contains Unicode line/paragraph separators instead of standard `\n\n`.

## Evidence

### Proof: standalone U+2029 splits at paragraph boundary

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
// Lone U+2029: must split (old code: stayed fused as one chunk)
const r = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one paragraph two starts here", 39);
console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
'
["paragraph one","paragraph two starts here"]
```

**Before fix**: standalone ` ` → `\n` (single LF) → blank-line detector `\n\n+` finds nothing → `["paragraph one\nparagraph two starts here"]` — **fused as one chunk**  
**After fix**: standalone ` ` → `\n\n` (blank line) → detector matches → `["paragraph one", "paragraph two starts here"]` — **splits at paragraph boundary**

### Proof: standalone U+2028 stays as intra-paragraph line break

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
const r = chunkByParagraph("line one line two same paragraph", 50);
console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
'
["line one\nline two same paragraph"]
```

**U+2028 → `\n` — single newline, no blank line → stays within one paragraph.** Matches standard `\n` behavior.

### Proof: consecutive U+2028  forms blank line

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
const unicode = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one line  paragraph two starts here", 40);
const newlines = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one line\n\nparagraph two starts here", 40);
console.log(JSON.stringify({unicode, newlines, match: unicode[0] === newlines[0] && unicode[1] === newlines[1]}));
'
{"unicode":["paragraph one line","paragraph two starts here"],"newlines":["paragraph one line","paragraph two starts here"],"match":true}
```

### Observed result

| Input | Behavior | Match \n\n? |
|-------|----------|------------|
| lone U+2029 | → `\n\n` → splits into 2 paragraphs | ✅ |
| lone U+2028 | → `\n` → stays in 1 paragraph | ✅ |
| U+2028  | → `\n\n\n` → splits into 2 paragraphs | ✅ |

### What was not tested

Live model output carrying real Unicode separators on a channel.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  71 passed (71)
```

```
$ npx oxlint src/auto-reply/chunk.ts src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts — exit 0
```

```
$ git diff upstream/main --stat — 2 files changed, 30 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

Three new tests:
1. Lone U+2029 → paragraph boundary (old test only covered consecutive U+2028 )
2. Lone U+2028 → single line break within paragraph
3. Consecutive U+2028  → combined blank line → identical output to \n\n

Branch rebased on upstream main.

## Root Cause

In `chunkByParagraph()` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts:209`), the normalization regex `/ \r\n?|[  ]/g` maps both U+2028 and U+2029 to a single `\n`. But paragraph detection requires a blank-line sequence `\n\n+`. Standalone U+2029 produces only one `\n`, so the blank-line detector never fires — the paragraph remains fused. The original test accidentally masked this because it placed U+2028 and U+2029 consecutively, producing two normalized `\n` characters that formed the required blank line. The fix uses a two-step normalization: U+2029 (= paragraph break) maps to `\n\n` first, then U+2028/U+2028/rn? (= line break) map to `\n`.
