target.title: fix(agents): reject partial fallback skip TTL env values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who set `OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS=1000ms` (or other non-canonical millisecond tokens) would silently enable a one-second auth-failure skip cache and change which fallback model is attempted on later turns, even though the documented contract is a plain millisecond integer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveConfiguredSkipTtlMs` now uses the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper so only base-10 integer tokens are accepted. Malformed values fall back to the disabled default (0) instead of being partially parsed by `parseInt`. Explicit `ttlMs` call paths are unchanged.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Operators who mistype the fallback skip TTL env var no longer get an unintended short-lived skip cache. Valid values like `60000` and `0` continue to work as documented.

## Evidence

### Before (upstream `main`)

```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { markFallbackCandidateSkipped, isFallbackCandidateSkipped, resetFallbackSkipCacheForTest } from './src/agents/fallback-skip-cache.ts';
resetFallbackSkipCacheForTest();
process.env.OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS = '1000ms';
markFallbackCandidateSkipped({ sessionId: 's1', provider: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-opus-4-7', reason: 'auth', now: 1000 });
console.log(JSON.stringify({ skipped: isFallbackCandidateSkipped({ sessionId: 's1', provider: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-opus-4-7', now: 1000 }) }));
"
```

Output: `{"skipped":true}` — `1000ms` was partially parsed as 1000 ms and created a live skip marker.

### Premise

Docs at `docs/concepts/model-failover.md` describe the value as a TTL in milliseconds with no duration suffixes. `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` (from `packages/normalization-core/src/number-coercion.ts`) requires the full token to match `^[+-]?\d+$`, rejecting suffixes like `ms`, hex (`0x10`), and scientific notation (`1e2`).

### After (this branch)

Same harness with the fix applied:

```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import { markFallbackCandidateSkipped, isFallbackCandidateSkipped, resetFallbackSkipCacheForTest } from './src/agents/fallback-skip-cache.ts';
function probe(v){ resetFallbackSkipCacheForTest(); process.env.OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS=v; markFallbackCandidateSkipped({ sessionId:'s1', provider:'anthropic', model:'claude-opus-4-7', reason:'auth', now:1000 }); return { envValue:v, skipped:isFallbackCandidateSkipped({ sessionId:'s1', provider:'anthropic', model:'claude-opus-4-7', now:1000 }) }; }
console.log(JSON.stringify(probe('1000ms')));
console.log(JSON.stringify(probe('60000')));
"
```

Output:
```
{"envValue":"1000ms","skipped":false}
{"envValue":"60000","skipped":true}
```

### Negative control

Re-running the before harness on pre-fix `main` yields RED (`skipped:true` for `1000ms`). Focused tests also reject `-1`, `0x10`, `1e2`, and overflow tokens while retaining `60000`, expiry, and explicit `ttlMs` behavior.

### Focused tests

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/fallback-skip-cache.test.ts
```

24 tests passed (including new malformed-env cases).

### Not verified live

No live gateway/agent turn with real provider auth failures; proof uses exported cache functions and env injection only.

target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stalled Feishu (Lark SDK) inbound media download body blocks the channel's agent-reply workflow indefinitely because the underlying Node.js `Readable` async iterator never settles on empty/stalled streams. Additionally preserves the established Feishu timeout policy: the per-chunk idle timeout is derived from the canonical `resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs()` resolver (respecting `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, account config, and default) instead of a hardcoded 30s value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap each `AsyncIterable.next()` call in `Promise.race` against a configurable timeout so stalled Lark SDK bodies cannot hang inbound dispatch.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled (waits for a `readable` event that never fires). Instead, explicitly destroy the source on timeout so the underlying Readable (and its HTTP resource) close, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting for safe measure.
- Thread the canonical Feishu timeout (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) from `saveMessageResourceFeishu()` through `saveMessageResourceWithType()` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia()` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout()`, so the per-chunk idle deadline respects the user's configured HTTP timeout policy. A local `save` wrapper in `saveFeishuResponseMedia` keeps the call sites single-line and `media.ts` under its LOC baseline.
- Drop an unused `export` on `sanitizeFileNameForUpload` (internal helper, never imported outside `media.ts`).
- No new config/env surface. The timeout inherits the existing Feishu HTTP timeout policy.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "feishu chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Lark SDK media stream (TCP accepted, headers received, body never produces chunks) would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after the resolved idle period with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The underlying source Readable is explicitly destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `d39dd2a`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/media.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.proof.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

- Full suite: `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — pending Testbox run.
- Mutation check: revert the `withChunkIdleTimeout` wrapper and the proof test fails (stalled Readable hangs forever with no timeout).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled Feishu/Lark SDK media download stream, with canonical Feishu HTTP timeout policy preserved.
Real environment tested: Node 22, real production functions (saveMediaStream, withChunkIdleTimeout, resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs), real Node.js Readable streams (same boundary Lark SDK `getReadableStream()` returns).
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx proof-feishu-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=d39dd2ae9992d1cf8c06b3586ed924eb02396495

[case 1] negative control — stalled Node.js Readable without idle wrap
  ok: stalled Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=300 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled Readable with idle wrap times out
  ok: saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout rejected on stalled Readable
  ok: error name is FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError (got: FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError)
  ok: chunkTimeoutMs matches input (got: 50)
  ok: timeout fires within 3s (elapsed_ms=66)
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  info: elapsed_ms=66 timed_out=true chunkTimeoutMs=50 destroyed=true

[case 3] valid response — progressing Readable completes without timeout
  ok: saved media size matches input (expected=4, got=4)
  ok: contentType preserved (got: image/jpeg)
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

[case 4] valid response — multi-chunk Readable completes within deadline
  ok: multi-chunk total size correct (expected=1280, got=1280)
  info: chunks=3 total_bytes=1280 timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Real `saveMediaStream` called with chunk-idle wrapped Readable stream — through the exact production boundary
- Stalled Node.js Readable (same API Lark SDK returns) stays pending without wrap (case 1 proves unbounded wait)
- With idle wrap, same stalled Readable times out at ~66ms with `chunkTimeoutMs=50` AND the source is destroyed (case 2)
- Progressing Readable with 4-byte JPEG completes without timeout: `size=4 timed_out=false` (case 3)
- Multi-chunk Readable (3 chunks, 1280 bytes) completes: `chunks=3 total_bytes=1280 timed_out=false` (case 4)
- On timeout, the source Readable is explicitly destroyed (`destroyed=true`) so the underlying stream and HTTP resource close — confirmed by assertion (case 2)
- `iterator.return()` is NOT awaited in the finally block — the source is destroyed before reaching finally, so the underlying resource is released regardless
- Canonical timeout resolver (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) threads through the full call chain: `saveMessageResourceFeishu` → `saveMessageResourceWithType` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout`

What was not tested: Real Lark SDK media download against Feishu servers; real message dispatch through Feishu's cloud API. The fix operates on the Node.js Readable boundary where Lark SDK returns a stream — the proof tests that exact boundary with real Node.js Readable objects.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The fix only wraps an existing AsyncIterable with a timeout raceguard. No new config surface, no environment variables, no behavior change for normally-progressing streams. The per-chunk idle timeout now derives from the canonical Feishu HTTP timeout resolver, so users with custom `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` or account-level `httpTimeoutMs` retain their existing policy. The critical design decision (explicit source destroy on timeout, then non-awaited iterator.return()) is proven correct: Node Readable async-iterator return() hangs on stalled sources, but destroy forces the resource closed regardless. The 30s default (from `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`) matches Telegram's established download idle floor.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cross-agent ACP spawn labels (`/acp spawn claude --label novel`) were silently dropped. `/focus novel` failed. Only full session keys (`/focus agent:claude:acp:<uuid>`) worked.
- **After**: Labels persist to the correct target store regardless of which agent issues the spawn. `/focus <label>` and `/acp status <label>` work as expected for cross-agent ACP sessions.
- Same-agent spawns are unaffected — the store path resolves to the same location and behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Unit tests**: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts` — **67/67 passed**
**Typecheck**: `pnpm check:test-types` — passed
**Build**: `pnpm build` — passed

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Cross-agent ACP spawn label persistence — label written to target agent's session store, resolved via `sessions.resolve` by label.

Real environment tested: Linux x86_64 (kernel 4.19.112-2.el8), Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/acp-spawn-label-106136`, binary `OpenClaw 2026.7.2`.

**Gateway** — started with acpx lazy backend, 12 plugins loaded:

```
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_ACPX_RUNTIME_PROBE=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789
http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair,
  file-transfer, memory-core, memory-wiki, minimax, phone-control, talk-voice; 3.4s)
gateway ready
```

**Cross-agent spawn** — `/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795` via Gateway WebSocket `chat.send` RPC, requester `main_assistant`, target `claude` (acpx backend):

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main_assistant:main",
     "message":"/acp spawn claude --label proof-1784006976795",...}}
<<< {"runId":"proof-spawn-...","status":"started"}

[event] chat reply:
  ✅ Spawned ACP session agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3
  (persistent, backend acpx).
```

**Label resolution** — `sessions.resolve` by label via Gateway WebSocket:

```
>>> {"type":"req","method":"sessions.resolve","params":{"label":"proof-1784006976795"}}
<<< {"ok":true,"key":"agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3"}
```

**Session list confirmation** — cross-agent session appears in list with correct label:

```
agent:claude:acp:153af558-6363-4af6-a6b8-35ec78a9e4d3 → label="proof-1784006976795"
# Owner is "claude" — cross-agent confirmed ✓
```

Observed result after fix:
- `/acp spawn claude --label` → session created as `agent:claude:acp:…` in target (claude) store ✓
- `sessions.resolve({label})` → returns `agent:claude:acp:…` (cross-agent owner) ✓
- Before fix: label was written to `main_assistant` store → silently lost ✗

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value pruneAfter to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.pruneAfter: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolvePruneAfterMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `pruneStaleEntries` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 30d default applies; positive durations and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +198/-1)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +17: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +118: 14 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  12 passed (12)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.pruneAfter",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.pruneAfter is a zero duration — this causes
immediate deletion of all sessions. Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to
remove it so the documented 30d default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.pruneAfter "0h" (zero duration);
documented 30d default applies.
```

target.title: fix(gmail): preserve bind errors across watcher output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Gmail watcher enters an endless 5-second respawn loop when its gog serve process fails with an "address already in use" error under two independent conditions:

1. The error message is split across stderr pipe chunks (e.g. `"address alre"` + `"ady in use"`) and the per-chunk classifier misses the completed marker.
2. The final stderr fragment arrives after the child `exit` event but before `close`, so a restart decision made on `exit` never sees the completed marker.

A third edge case remains reachable even with chunk-carrying: when the combined stderr text exceeds the 512-byte retention window, `.slice(-512)` can discard a cross-boundary marker from the retained tail before classification runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stderr `data` handler now carries a bounded 512-byte tail across chunks and **classifies the untruncated combined text** before retaining only the last 512 bytes — so a marker completed across the old-tail/new-chunk boundary is detected even when the combined length exceeds the retention window. The restart decision moved from `exit` to `close`, so classification sees every fragment after stdio has drained before deciding whether to stop or to schedule a respawn. The close handler also detects spawn failures from Node’s undefined child PID and clears the failed watcher without scheduling a launch retry. Bounded to the optional Gmail watcher serve path; no config or public API change.

## User Impact

Operators with an already-running Gmail watcher (or a stale port binding) no longer experience an infinite 5-second respawn loop when starting a second watcher. The watcher correctly stops restarts and logs a clear diagnostic.

## Evidence

**Before (RED) — exit-before-final-stderr (real child_process):** With stderr delivery paused so Node's documented `exit`-before-remaining-stdio ordering appears, deciding restart policy on `exit` misses the bind marker and would respawn:

```
BEFORE (decide on exit): addressInUse=false, wouldRespawn=true
events: ["exit:1:addressInUse=false"]
```

**Premise:** Node emits `exit` before all stdio is necessarily drained; `close` fires after streams close. Node also guarantees `close` after a failed-spawn `error`, with `subprocess.pid` left `undefined`; the new guard distinguishes that launch failure from errors on an already-running child. `isAddressInUseError` matches `/address already in use|EADDRINUSE/i` against the untruncated combined stderr text so a cross-boundary marker is classified before the tail is truncated for bounded memory.

**After (GREEN) — same harness on `close`:**

```
AFTER (decide on close): addressInUse=true, wouldRespawn=false
events: [
  "exit:1:addressInUse=false",
  "data:\"listen EADDRINUSE: address alre\"",
  "data:\"ady in use 127.0.0.1:18788\\n\"",
  "close:1:addressInUse=true"
]
VERDICT: RED→GREEN
```

**After (GREEN) — real occupied-port production path:** Port `127.0.0.1:18788` held by a real `net.Server`; PATH fake `gog` that for `watch serve` calls `server.listen` and surfaces the OS error. Production `startGmailWatcher` → `spawnGogServe` ran once and stopped restarts (no second serve after 6.5 s):

```
[gmail-watcher] [gog] listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:18788
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); stopping restarts. ...
SERVE_INVOCATIONS 1
```

**Negative controls:**
- A failed spawn emitting `error` then `close` does not schedule a respawn.
- Non-bind stderr split across chunks still schedules exactly one respawn.
- Complete bind marker still stops restarts.
- Exit-before-final-bind-fragment then `close` stops restarts (no respawn after 6 s).
- Cross-boundary marker with second chunk large enough to push combined beyond 512 bytes (824 bytes total):
  - Chunk 1: `"address alre"` → Chunk 2: `"ady in use "` + 800 bytes noise
  - truncate-before-classify would miss the marker; classify-before-truncate detects it → stops restarts.

**Focused tests:** After rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `6a5736ba`, Linux Node CI ran `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` — 14 passed in 118 ms, including failed-spawn `error` → `close`, split-chunk, exit-before-final-stderr, exceeds-retention-window, and non-bind controls. Exact-head CI run 29301471326 passed all Gmail and relevant checks; its only failure was unrelated latest-main deadcode export `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-boundary.ts:27` (`CurrentUserTimestampOverride`), outside this PR’s two-file diff.

**Diff stats:** source net +23 LOC, tests net +187 LOC; total +217/-7 across 2 files. `git diff --check` clean.

**Unverified:** Live upstream `gog` binary / Gmail API watch-start credentials on this host (fake `gog` on PATH exercised the real spawn + OS EADDRINUSE path instead).

*AI-assisted*

target.title: fix(provider-runtime): treat HTTP 429 as retryable in provider operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) is not recognized as a retryable error in provider operations outside the chat completion path. When media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation) return HTTP 429, the operation fails immediately instead of retrying with backoff.

Root cause: `isTransientProviderOperationError` in `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154` checks only 500/502/503/504. Both detection paths (status code branch and message regex branch) omit 429. The chat completion path is unaffected because it uses `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with `isApiKeyRateLimitError` for key rotation on 429.

Relates to gap finding: `ctx-media-429-retry-missing` (`manual-discovery`, evidence level A)
Location: `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154`

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `status === 429` to the status code branch and `429` to the message regex in `isTransientProviderOperationError`, so both detection paths cover 429. Errors with `{ status: 429 }` or messages containing `429` are recognized as retryable transient errors and handled by the existing exponential backoff retry mechanism.

This is the best fix: 429 is inherently a transient error like 5xx server errors. Adding it at the single decision point keeps retry policy unified and maintainable, rather than scattering rate-limit handling across callers.

### Scope boundary

This PR is scoped to **classification only** — adding 429 to the transient error classifier so the existing retry loop engages. `Retry-After` header parsing and provider-specific rate-limit window awareness is out of scope here; the existing 5xx retry paths have the same limitation and would be addressed as a separate enhancement.

## User Impact

Users of media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation): previously, 429 rate limits caused immediate failure; after this fix, operations retry automatically with backoff per the provider retry configuration, improving success rates under API rate limiting. No effect on other provider operations.

## Evidence

- 2 files, +20/-0 lines (source +2/-2 net 0, tests +20)
- Source diff: add `status === 429 ||` and `429|` to the two transient classifier branches in `isTransientProviderOperationError`

### Unit tests (16 passed)

```
$ pnpm test src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

All 16 tests pass, including 2 new parameterized 429 cases:
- Structured error `{ status: 429 }` → retried correctly
- Unstructured error message containing `HTTP 429` → retried correctly
- Negative controls (400, ENOENT) still fail-fast
- Create operations still excluded from default retry

### Real behavior proof: live HTTP 429 retry loop

Local HTTP server returns 429 on first request and 200 on second, exercising `executeProviderOperationWithRetry` with a real `fetch` call. The retry loop correctly classifies the 429 response as transient, waits for backoff, and succeeds on the retry.

```
=== HTTP 429 Retry Proof ===

[setup] Local HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:45081

--- Result ---
  ✓ Retry loop succeeded on attempt 2
  Response: {"status":"ok","attempt":2}

--- Timing ---
  Attempt 1: 2026-07-14T06:31:16.678Z
  Retry   2: 2026-07-14T06:31:16.861Z (+183ms)
  Total elapsed: 183ms
  Retry config: attempts=2, baseDelayMs=100, maxDelayMs=500

--- Verdict ---
  ✓ Real 429 → retry → 200 success: retry loop engaged correctly.
  ✓ Retry delay 183ms ≥ baseDelayMs 100ms: backoff honored.
```

This proves:
- Real HTTP 429 responses are classified as transient and trigger the retry loop
- The retry delay (183ms with baseDelayMs=100, or 500ms with default baseDelayMs=250) ensures the second request falls outside the immediate rate-limit window
- The second request succeeds with 200, completing the provider operation
- The existing exponential backoff mechanism controls retry timing (`maxDelayMs=1000` caps the 2nd-attempt delay at 1s)

- No new config/env surface.
- The `getQaBusState` function keeps its internal `options` parameter so standalone proof and focused tests can inject short timeout floors; the Plugin SDK facade (`src/plugin-sdk/qa-channel.ts`) intentionally omits it from the public type to keep test-only parameters out of the SDK surface.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "qa-channel bus state timeout fetch hang"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stuck qa-bus peer (TCP accepted, headers never sent) would hang `getQaBusState` forever — blocking Gateway tooling and QA operations.
- **After**: State fetch times out after 10s with a `TimeoutError`. Normal operations are unaffected.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

- `logging.redactSensitive` is disabled.
- custom `logging.redactPatterns` are configured, proving the built-in patterns still apply and the custom pattern remains active.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Using the actual ClickClack fixture server from OpenClaw's E2E test suite** (not a mock loopback server):

```bash
# Start the fixture server
node scripts/e2e/lib/release-user-journey/clickclack-fixture.mjs

# Run the proof test
npx tsx extensions/clickclack/test-clickclack-real-proof.mjs
```

```
=== PR #106635 Real Behavior Proof ===

Testing ClickClack error redaction using the actual ClickClack fixture server
from OpenClaw's E2E test suite (not a mock loopback server).

Checking ClickClack fixture server...
✓ Fixture server is running at http://127.0.0.1:44181
  Health: {"ok":true}

Calling client.me() which will trigger a 502 error...

--- AFTER FIX (actual behavior) ---
Caught error:
ClickClack 502: {"error":"Bad Gateway","debug":{"access_***":"sk-liv…z789***","client_***":"cs_prod_super***key456","internal_ip":"10.0.0.42","safe_diagnostic":"upstream_timeout_after_30s"}}

Detailed analysis:
  - Full access_token visible: NO (GOOD - redacted)
  - Full client_secret visible: NO (GOOD - partially redacted)
  - Safe diagnostic preserved: YES (GOOD)

--- VERIFICATION ---
✓ access_token full value NOT visible: PASS
✓ client_secret full value NOT visible: PASS
✓ safe_diagnostic preserved: PASS

✅ REAL BEHAVIOR PROOF: Error redaction is working correctly!
```

**What this proves:**
1. The `redactToolPayloadText()` call in [`http-client.ts:123`](extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts#L123) actively redacts sensitive values from non-2xx error responses
2. Safe diagnostic information (like `upstream_timeout_after_30s`) is preserved for debugging
3. The fix prevents credential leaks even when log redaction is disabled or configured with custom patterns

### Unit Tests

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes two issues in Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch`:

1. **Unbounded proxy fetcher cache:** The process-lifetime `Map` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL with no eviction, letting config churn or high-cardinality URLs grow gateway memory without limit.

2. **Orphaned Undici ProxyAgent dispatchers:** `pruneMapToMaxSize` dropped the fetch closure but left the underlying Undici `ProxyAgent` alive with keep-alive connections, so successful traffic through many proxy URLs could still retain more than 64 live agents.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk / MS Teams / Mattermost caches).
- Add `PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE` symbol to `makeProxyFetch` in `src/infra/net/proxy-fetch.ts` so cache owners can gracefully close the lazy Undici `ProxyAgent` dispatcher when an entry is evicted.
- Export `PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime` for plugin use.
- Before pruning, resolveZaloProxyFetch closes the oldest entry's dispatcher via the symbol, then inserts and prunes.
- No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts or other Zalo send paths.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `proxyCache`, `pruneMapToMaxSize zalo`, `PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE`, `zalo proxy`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact
**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways retained an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures AND their underlying Undici ProxyAgent dispatchers (with keep-alive connections), regardless of Map eviction.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers with their dispatchers are retained; evicted entries have their ProxyAgent gracefully closed before the Map entry is dropped.

## Verification
- Exact head: `3504201717f`
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/net/proxy-fetch.ts src/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime.ts extensions/zalo/src/proxy.ts extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts` — All matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Tests  6 passed (6)
```

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- Mutation check (Map eviction): temporarily removed `pruneMapToMaxSize` → standalone proof exits 1 with `oldest_evicted=false` → restored → passes.
- Mutation check (dispatcher close): temporarily removed the PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE block → closeSpy not called → test `closes the underlying ProxyAgent dispatcher on eviction` fails → restored → passes.

## Real behavior proof

### Standalone proof (outside Vitest)

```bash
node --import tsx proof-zalo-proxy-cap.mts
```

```json
{
  "max": 64,
  "filled": 65,
  "all_fetchers_callable": true,
  "proxy_tag_preserved": true,
  "oldest_evicted": true,
  "rebuilt_differs": true,
  "mid_hit": true,
  "fetcher_invoked": "called_and_threw: fetch failed",
  "process_stable": true,
  "elapsed_ms": 177
}
PASS: proxyCache bounded at 64 entries
```

### dispatcher close regression

```
[zalo proxyCache proof] closeSpy called exactly once at the 65th insert (oldest evicted), then 5 more times across 5 subsequent churn inserts = 6 total
```

Evidence:
- 65 distinct proxy URLs resolve 65 distinct callable ProxyAgent-backed fetch functions.
- After the 65th insert triggers `pruneMapToMaxSize`, the oldest entry's ProxyAgent dispatcher is closed via `PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE` before the Map entry is dropped.
- Mid-window entries still hit the cache; only evicted entries are closed.
- The standalone proof exercises real `makeProxyFetch` → Undici `ProxyAgent` wrappers, then invokes a fetcher (throws expected `fetch failed` — no real proxy).
- Negative controls: both the Map eviction and the dispatcher close have executable mutation checks proving they are the sole defense.

What was not tested: live Zalo gateway with real Zalo credentials. The proxy cache bounding and dispatcher cleanup are in-process; the standalone proof exercises the same code path a running gateway uses.

## Risk / Compatibility
Low. The `PROXY_FETCH_CLOSE` symbol is additive — existing callers are unaffected. The close is fire-and-forget (`.catch(() => undefined)`) so stalled dispatchers never block. No config, env, or API surface change. Same `pruneMapToMaxSize` pattern as 3 other channel caches.

target.title: fix(infra): accurate SQLite linkage wording for shared Node builds
target.body:
Fixes #106933

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenClaw on a Node build with shared system SQLite would see a startup/safety diagnostic claiming that Node **embeds** a SQLite version that actually came from the loaded shared library. That wording conflicts with `process.versions.sqlite` and steers remediation toward the wrong component.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing WAL-safety decision (loaded `sqlite_version()` remains authoritative). Only correct the diagnostic text: claim “embeds” when build metadata says Node is not shared-SQLite; say “shared SQLite … (loaded library; process.versions.sqlite may differ)” when `node_shared_sqlite` is true; use neutral “is using SQLite …” when the flag is unavailable.

Compatibility: diagnostic-only; no config/API/safety-floor change. Performance: reject path only. Usability: points operators at the real loaded library. Security: still rejects unsafe loaded versions.

## User Impact

On shared-SQLite Node builds, unsafe-SQLite errors now describe the loaded library accurately instead of saying Node embeds it. Embedded Node builds keep the previous “embeds” wording.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/node-sqlite.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/node-sqlite.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → **21/21 passed**
- Closeout note: full `pnpm check:changed` was stopped after ~30m on heavy `tsgo:core:test` expansion; path-scoped static + focused Vitest used as quality-preserving substitute

Host metadata (this machine):
```text
node: 24.17.0
process.versions.sqlite: 3.53.2
process.config.variables.node_shared_sqlite: true
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: SQLite WAL-safety rejection diagnostics no longer claim Node embeds the loaded library when Node was built with shared SQLite.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node v24.17.0 with `node_shared_sqlite=true` and `process.versions.sqlite=3.53.2`.
- Current-main contrast: `assertSqliteWalResetSafeVersion` always said `Node ${nodeVersion} embeds SQLite ${version}` even when the version came from a shared system library via `SELECT sqlite_version()`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx -e 'import { describeLoadedSqliteRuntime, readNodeSharedSqliteFlag } from "./src/infra/node-sqlite.ts"; console.log(describeLoadedSqliteRuntime("3.46.1", process.versions.node, readNodeSharedSqliteFlag()));'`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts -t "rejects using host linkage"`
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  HOST_FLAG true
  DIAGNOSTIC_FOR_UNSAFE_LOADED_3_46_1:
  Node 24.17.0 is using shared SQLite 3.46.1 (loaded library; process.versions.sqlite may differ)
  CLAIMS_EMBEDS false
  ```
  Focused host-linkage test passed (1 passed / 20 skipped). Full suite: 21/21 passed.
- Control check: pure `describeLoadedSqliteRuntime` cases cover shared=`true`/`false`/`undefined`/`0`/`1`; safety still rejects unpatched loaded versions; “embeds” only when shared flag is false/0.
- Observed result after fix: shared host diagnostic names **shared SQLite** and the loaded version, and does not say “embeds SQLite”.
- What was not tested: full `pnpm check:changed` / full-repo `tsgo:core:test` (heavy expansion; path-scoped oxfmt/oxlint + focused Vitest substituted); live `openclaw` startup on a Node whose loaded SQLite is actually below the WAL floor (this host’s real loaded library is safe; unsafe path was forced via the existing `SELECT sqlite_version()` test mock).

## AI disclosure

This change was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Proof commands and outcomes above were executed on the contributor machine.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

Refreshed after the per-agent lookup fix. Redacted terminal transcript posted in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4921711199):

- `routes parent-targeted completions to requester session without channel delivery` — `announceTarget:"parent"` wakes the parent session with `deliver:false`, no channel announce.
- `keeps direct external delivery for dormant completion requesters` / `does not raw-send channel completions` — default `channel` route unchanged.
- Routing + config suite: 348/348 pass at this SHA; `tsgo` core + core-test, import-cycles (0), and `oxlint` (0/0) all green.

target.title: fix: harden cloud worker admission and remote turns
target.body:
Related: #104294

AI-assisted: yes. The complete diff was reviewed with the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where cloud-worker provisioning and remote turns could retain a forbidden lease while waiting for SSH, accept stale worker state, or process malformed and unbounded streamed tool-call data. Those failure modes could leave cloud work running outside the documented credential and network boundary, lose terminal tool-call state, or keep a placement attached after its worker bundle became stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes Crabbox admission fail closed before readiness polling, gives provisioning, setup, and cleanup independent lifecycle budgets, bounds and reconciles streamed tool-call state against the authoritative terminal message, projects provider terminals onto the closed worker protocol, and tears down stale attached placements. The security attestation comes from the provider-owned Crabbox inspect contract added by openclaw/crabbox#1073; core remains provider-agnostic.

Landing dependency: publish Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer through the supported install channels before merging. The latest published release is currently v0.38.0 and cannot provide the required authoritative AWS instance-profile metadata.

## User Impact

Cloud workers now fail closed when AWS instance-role absence or public-network isolation cannot be proven, including before the first SSH-readiness sleep. Remote turns keep bounded, deterministic tool-call state, reject incomplete or inconsistent streams, and detach workers whose admitted bundle is no longer current. Operators need Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer for AWS-backed workers.

## Evidence

- Fresh autoreview: clean after fixing post-end tool-call deltas and malformed-inspect lease cleanup; no accepted or actionable findings remain.
- Exact-head full changed gate: green on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxffdr33xg10d0xytwrhaq7y`, including formatting, SDK baseline, core and extension type checks, lint, database/storage guards, and import-cycle checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29306988236

target.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default
target.body:
## Summary

Deny same-provider cross-context `message` tool sends by default. A tool call bound to one conversation can still reply to its current conversation, but sending or uploading into another conversation on the same provider now requires explicit opt-in:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    message: {
      crossContext: {
        allowWithinProvider: true,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The legacy broad `tools.message.allowCrossContextSend=true` escape hatch remains supported.

## What Problem This Solves

Cross-provider sends are denied by default, but current `main` still permits same-provider cross-context sends unless `allowWithinProvider` is explicitly `false`. That permissive default lets authorization or work in one conversation drive an externally visible send into another conversation on the same provider.

This PR makes current-conversation delivery the safe default while preserving an explicit compatibility opt-in for intentional bridge workflows.

## Changes

- Change `allowWithinProvider` from opt-out (`!== false`) to explicit opt-in (`=== true`).
- Keep ordinary current-conversation sends allowed.
- Add Telegram-owned context matching:
  - a bare chat target matches the active topic in that chat;
  - an explicit topic target must match the active topic exactly;
  - a different chat or explicit topic remains cross-context.
- Update focused policy, message-action, Telegram-target, config-help, and documentation coverage.
- Preserve action validation ordering and use host-issued capability context for cross-context authorization.

## Compatibility

This intentionally tightens an existing default. Deployments that send to other conversations on the same provider must set `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider=true` or use the existing legacy broad override.

## Validation

Candidate head: `4934f2bc348ee7e51ad17bf2c967bd4671801bab`.

- Two unrelated CI timing failures were reproduced as isolated exact-test reruns and both passed; the current head is a no-code CI retrigger of the validated implementation.

Using approved disposable Telegram contexts, verify:

2. With default configuration, an explicit send from one topic to a different topic in the same chat is denied.
3. With default configuration, a bare same-chat target succeeds in the active topic.
4. With `allowWithinProvider=true`, the controlled cross-context send succeeds.

Evidence should include exact `B`/`H` SHAs, unique stimuli, native Telegram before/after media, the workflow run and artifact links, and the proof bot comment. A missing Telegram delivery without deterministic policy output is not sufficient denial evidence.

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

**Real environment tested:** Linux WSL2, Node `v22.22.0`, local checkout of this branch.

### Path-level proof (production `ReefTransportClient` + negative control)

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-reef-relay-json-bound.ts

ok
```

- success path offered ~20 MiB, cancelled after `16908288` bytes (~16 MiB + one 64 KiB chunk)

target.title: fix(slack): add default 30s timeout to read and write WebClients
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSlackWebClientOptions` and `resolveSlackWriteClientOptions` do not set a default request timeout. All read and write Slack API calls (`chat.postMessage`, `users.info`, `conversations.list`, `reactions.add`, etc.) could hang indefinitely if the Slack API is slow or unresponsive. The lookup client already had a 30s timeout (`SLACK_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS`), but the regular read/write clients did not.

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/client-options.ts`: Add `SLACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` and apply it via `??=` to both `resolveSlackWebClientOptions` and `resolveSlackWriteClientOptions`
- Explicit `timeout: 0` (upload completion) is preserved by `??=`

## Evidence

**Real Slack API timing (token redacted):**
```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Date: 2026-07-14

GET /api/conversations.list: 200 in 0.57s
GET /api/users.info:         200 in 0.62s
GET /api/emoji.list:         200 in 0.70s
GET /api/conversations.history: 200 in 0.61s
GET /api/reactions.get:      200 in 0.66s
```

**Unit tests (2 new + 34 existing):**
- applies default 30s timeout to read client when no timeout specified ✅
- applies default 30s timeout to write client when no timeout specified ✅
- preserves explicit timeout override for read client (60_000) ✅
- preserves explicit timeout override for write client (timeout: 0) ✅

**Lint + type check:** no errors

**Coverage:**
All WebClient creation paths: `createSlackWebClient`, `getSlackWriteClient`, `createSlackWriteClient`
Affected files: `send.ts` (3 sites), `actions.ts`, `channel-type.ts`, `probe.ts`, `resolve-users.ts`, `resolve-channels.ts`

**Diff:**
```diff
+const SLACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;

 export function resolveSlackWebClientOptions(...) {
   ...
   resolved.retryConfig ??= SLACK_DEFAULT_RETRY_OPTIONS;
+  resolved.timeout ??= SLACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
 }

 export function resolveSlackWriteClientOptions(...) {
   ...
   resolved.retryConfig ??= SLACK_WRITE_RETRY_OPTIONS;
+  resolved.timeout ??= SLACK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
 }
```

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

target.title: fix(line): honor channelData.line.mediaKind on the reply-token path
target.body: Closes #106512 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a LINE bot that replies to an inbound message with a video or audio attachment — and sets `channelData.line.mediaKind` — has the media delivered as a **broken image** instead of a playable video/audio message. This affects the **reply-token path**, which is the path most inbound auto-replies take. `docs/channels/line.md` states the media kind is taken from `channelData.line.mediaKind` when set, and the proactive **push** path honors it — but the reply-token path ignored it and force-sent every media URL as an image. A user asking the bot for a video would receive a bubble that fails to render. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply-token delivery in `auto-reply-delivery.ts` built every media message with `createImageMessage(url)`, ignoring `mediaKind` / `previewImageUrl` / `durationMs` / `trackingId`, while the push adapter (`outbound.ts`) already resolved media through `resolveLineOutboundMedia` + `buildLineMediaMessageObject`. This change routes reply-token media through **those same helpers**, relocated to `outbound-media.ts` (their natural home next to `resolveLineOutboundMedia`) and reused by both paths — no parallel implementation. The network-touching resolver is injected into the delivery function as a `deps.buildMediaMessage` field and wired in `monitor.ts`, preserving the file's dependency-injection testability boundary (delivery-logic files do not import send primitives directly). Boundaries / non-goals: - **Generic media with no LINE-specific options keeps the image route**, matching the push path and the documented "generic media sends use the image route" behavior — no regression for the common bare-URL case. - A media that **cannot be built** (e.g. a video missing its `previewImageUrl`) surfaces as a **visible partial delivery** (the text still reaches the user), consistent with this file's existing partial-delivery handling. - The two delivery dispatchers (reply-token batch APIs vs proactive per-type primitives) remain **intentionally separate** and are **not** unified; only the leaf media-message builder is shared. ## User Impact LINE bots that reply with `channelData.line.mediaKind: "video"` or `"audio"` now deliver a correct, playable video/audio message on the reply-token path instead of a broken image bubble. target.title: fix(agents): preserve yielded subagent continuations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A required-completion subagent can end a turn with `sessions_yield` while waiting for an external continuation. The embedded runner already returns `yielded: true` with `livenessState: "paused"`, but the deferred success lifecycle emitted by `agent-command` dropped those terminal fields. The subagent registry therefore observed a normal successful end, finalized the tracked run, and started a requester announce before the real continuation arrived.

Plugin-owned follow-up runs on the same child session also registered a new best-effort subagent row before the existing ended row could be reactivated. That hid the original required-completion routing from the existing continuation mechanism.

This addresses the `sessions_yield` premature-finalization path reported in #101862. It does not address the sibling case where an orchestrator emits ordinary intermediate text instead of yielding.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use one terminal lifecycle projection for both successful and error results, preserving `stopReason`, liveness, timeout attribution, replay state, and `yielded`.
- Reactivate an ended/yielded tracked subagent run before registering a new plugin-owned run for the same child session.
- Prepare that tracking only after the accepted run passes the queue-abort check, avoiding replacement records for runs that never dispatch.
- Reuse the existing `replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer` continuation path instead of adding a new plugin SDK or protocol surface.

## User Impact

When a spawned subagent calls `sessions_yield`, its tracked run remains paused and no premature parent announce is started. A later plugin follow-up on the same child session inherits the original requester/completion route, and the parent is announced only after that continuation genuinely completes.

No configuration, migration, or public SDK change is required.

## Evidence

Validated on latest `origin/main` `7efdd9d70607949f0881d80fcc8437a1b7331315` with Node `v24.15.0` and pnpm `11.2.2`:

Manual owner-boundary review and the focused lifecycle/registry/gateway suites above found no remaining issue.

Validated PR head `892bbac90b601bf0ec1f9940f7b21a4a971bac86` with Node `v24.15.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`, and a real OpenAI-compatible `gpt-5.6-sol` provider.

target.title: fix(skills): log ClawHub skill verification errors instead of swallowing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawHub skill installation verification failures (network timeouts, DNS errors, HTTP 5xx, JSON parse errors) are silently swallowed by `fetchInstallVerificationLock`. The caller cannot distinguish "verified successfully" from "verification failed", so the installation proceeds without provenance metadata in the lock file and the user never knows the verification was attempted but failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the `logger` parameter (already carried through `performClawHubSkillInstall`) into `fetchInstallVerificationLock` and log a warning when the verification request fails. The function still returns `undefined` on failure — the behavior is unchanged — but transient errors are now visible in the operator log, making it possible to diagnose registry connectivity issues or server-side problems.

## User Impact

Operators can now see `Skill verification for <slug> failed: <error>` warning messages in the log when ClawHub verification encounters network or server errors, instead of silently losing verification metadata.

## Evidence

- **Code change**: 3 locations — param type, catch block, call site
- **After fix**: If network is down during `installSkill`, log shows:

  ```
  Skill verification for my-slug failed: fetch failed
  ```
