target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed: 20 tests.

The body-stall case sent response headers and left the body open, then failed through `MediaFetchError`; the slow-progress case used `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 60` and kept sending chunks for 529ms, proving there is no complete-operation deadline cutting off a healthy transfer that continues to make progress.

target.title: fix(ui): apply Context Profile presets via config.patch to avoid SecretRef rejection
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Control UI Context Profile save fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` when the gateway config contains a redacted SecretRef. The previous implementation used `stageConfigPreset` to merge preset patches into the full editable configuration draft via `applyMergePatch`, then submitted the entire merged config through the shared `serializeFormForSubmit` → `submitConfigChange` → `config.set`/`config.apply` pipeline. When any `SecretRef` field (for example, a webhook route secret at `plugins.entries.webhooks.config.routes.internal-events.secret`) is redacted in the Control UI form, the gateway rejects the full-config submission because the redacted representation changes the `source` and `provider` fields without including an explicit `id` that identifies which secret is being updated. The gateway error message is `SecretRef at <path> changed source/provider while id is redacted. Provide an explicit id when changing source/provider.` This blocked ALL configuration changes submitted through Save or Apply Now, even changes to completely unrelated fields like `agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars`, because the full config serialization included the redacted secret fields. Users with any SecretRef-backed plugin configuration were unable to use the Control UI to modify any settings whatsoever through the Save or Apply Now workflow. A CLI workaround existed by writing individual fields via `openclaw config set`, but the Control UI profile workflow was completely broken for affected configurations.

**Solution**: Re-add Context Profile presets with four curated profiles: Personal Assistant with a moderate prompt budget suitable for daily chat and documentation use, Code Agent with the largest context budget optimized for multi-file repository work and code-heavy sessions, Team Bot with lean follow-up behavior designed for shared multi-channel bots where continuity matters more than large bootstrap payloads, and Minimal with the smallest context budget for cost-sensitive quick utility turns and automation workflows. Each preset application now submits only the three `agents.defaults` fields via the gateway's existing `config.patch` partial-write remote procedure call. The `config.patch` API accepts a base hash for optimistic concurrency control and a raw patch object containing only the fields to be modified. It applies these fields as a JSON merge patch to the stored gateway configuration without touching unrelated paths such as plugin entries, channel configurations, or SecretRef-backed secrets. This completely bypasses the full-form serialization pipeline which includes `serializeFormForSubmit`, `coerceFormValues`, and `sanitizeRedactedFormForSubmit`. The general Save and Apply Now path using `config.set` and `config.apply` remains unchanged for full-config editing scenarios where the user is editing the complete form or raw JSON configuration. Inline success and error feedback is displayed beside the preset controls after each application, using the same `renderSettingsStatus` component with danger tone for errors. The preset application state is tracked via `presetApplying` which disables the Apply button during the request to prevent double submissions, and `presetError` which captures the last error from the runtime config state for display alongside the preset cards.

**What changed**: Five files modified with a total of 211 line additions and 1 line deletion across the Control UI source tree. A new file `ui/src/pages/config/presets.ts` was created containing 107 lines with four preset definitions, the `ConfigPresetId` union type, the `ConfigPresetPatch` type describing the three owned fields, the `ConfigPreset` interface, the `CONFIG_PRESETS` constant array, and a `getPresetById` lookup function. The `ui/src/lib/config/index.ts` runtime config capability module received 15 new lines adding the `applyPreset` method declaration to the `RuntimeConfigCapability` type interface, a new `applyPresetConfig` async function that wraps the existing `patchConfig` function and calls `loadConfig` to refresh the config snapshot after a successful patch, and wiring the method into the capability factory's returned object. The `ui/src/pages/config/config-page.ts` Lit element received 29 new lines including imports for `getPresetById` and `ConfigPresetId`, two new reactive state properties `presetApplying` and `presetError` decorated with the Lit `@state` decorator, a new private `applyPreset` async method that looks up the preset by identifier, sets the applying and error state, calls `runtimeConfig.applyPreset` with the preset patch object and a human-readable note, handles both rejection and error state from `runtimeConfig.state.lastError`, and finally resets the applying state in a finally block, plus four new props passed to the `renderQuickSettings` call for `activePresetId`, `presetApplying`, `presetError`, and `onApplyPreset`. The `ui/src/pages/config/quick.ts` Quick Settings view module received 59 new lines and 1 removed blank line including imports for `CONFIG_PRESETS` and `ConfigPresetId`, four new optional props on the `QuickSettingsProps` type for preset integration, a new `renderContextProfileSection` function that maps over `CONFIG_PRESETS` to produce preset cards with icon header, active badge when the preset matches the current config state, description text, detail and impact muted text, an Apply button that disables during config busy or preset application states and shows an applying label during submission, a status indicator during application, and an error block using `renderSettingsStatus` with danger tone and ARIA alert role for accessibility, and the wiring of `renderContextProfileSection` as the first section in the `renderQuickSettings` main render function before the Model and Thinking section. The `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts` English locale file received 6 new lines adding a `presets` section under `quickSettings` with four translation keys for the section title Context Profile, the Apply button label, the Applying status label, and the Active badge label.

**What was NOT changed**: The general Save and Apply Now form submission path remains completely untouched. target.title: fix(control-ui): restore native context menu when text is selected (#106765)
target.body: Closes #106765 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users who select text inside a chat message bubble and right-click would only see the custom Reply menu instead of the browser's native context menu. This prevented users from using standard right-click actions such as Copy, Search with their default search engine, spell-check, and other browser-integrated tools on selected chat text. ## Why This Change Was Made The `handleChatContextMenu` handler in the chat thread unconditionally called `event.preventDefault()` whenever a right-click occurred on a chat bubble with an active `onSetReply` callback, suppressing the native context menu in all cases. The fix introduces a selection-aware escape hatch: when `window.getSelection()` reports a non-collapsed selection whose range is contained within the clicked bubble, the handler returns early without calling `preventDefault()`, allowing the browser's native context menu to appear. When no text is selected, the existing custom Reply menu behavior is preserved unchanged. **Non-goal:** This change does not add a custom Copy action to the Reply menu, nor does it introduce a configuration toggle. The approach defers to the browser's native menu, which includes Copy, Search, spell-check, and accessibility integrations that a custom action cannot fully replace. ## User Impact - **Selected text + right-click:** The browser's native context menu now appears (Copy, Search, spell-check, etc.), restoring expected browser behavior. - **No selection + right-click:** The custom Reply menu continues to appear as before. - **No configuration changes:** The fix is automatic and opt-out is not required (users who never select text will never notice the change). ## Evidence ### Before: selected text + right-click shows only the Reply menu (no Copy/Search) Before: selected text right-click shows only Reply menu ### After: selected text + right-click shows the native browser context menu After: selected text right-click shows native browser menu ### After: no selection + right-click still shows the Reply menu (regression guard) After: no selection right-click still shows Reply menu ### Tests ```bash # Targeted tests (2 new, 13 total in right-click Reply suite) $ pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts -t "right-click Reply" ✓ |unit| src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts (178 tests | 165 skipped) 324ms Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 13 passed | 165 skipped (178) # Full chat module regression (280 tests) $ pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --project unit src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts ✓ |unit| src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts (102 tests) 162ms ✓ |unit| src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts (178 tests) 2325ms Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 280 passed (280) ``` Additional new test coverage: - `preserves the native context menu when text is selected inside the bubble` — mocks a non-collapsed `getSelection()` range within the bubble and asserts `event.defaultPrevented === false` with no custom menu rendered - `shows the Reply menu when clicking without a text selection` — mocks a collapsed/null selection and asserts `event.defaultPrevented === true` with the custom Reply menu rendered --- This PR is AI-assisted. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MS Teams group/channel file sends that could hang indefinitely when SharePoint upload, sharing-link creation, chat-member lookup, or drive-item metadata requests stalled before headers or while reading response bodies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected SharePoint/Graph calls now use an aborting timeout around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The timeout helper lives in `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner.

SharePoint content PUTs now use the same size-aware transfer policy as the adjacent MS Teams file-consent upload path: a 5 minute base stall bound plus transfer budget at 256 KiB/s. Short Graph control-plane requests keep the existing 30 second MS Teams request timeout so stalled metadata/link/member calls still fail quickly without cutting off slow but valid file uploads.

## User Impact

MS Teams group/channel file sends no longer remain pending forever when Microsoft Graph or SharePoint stops responding. Slow valid large uploads get a transfer-sized deadline instead of being cut off by a fixed 5 minute ceiling or the 30 second control-plane timeout.

## Evidence

Exact head: `5a4dc3f94616aab7df490411c3237242aa0ca932`.

target.title: fix(skills): enforce byte-level cap on skill package downloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where skill package downloads via `pipeline(response.body, file)` have no byte-level cap. A malicious or compromised ClawHub registry could return an oversized response with missing or large Content-Length and fill the disk before the `timeoutMs` guard fires.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two layers of protection:
1. **Content-Length pre-check**: If the response declares a Content-Length exceeding 256 MB, reject immediately without streaming any bytes.
2. **Streaming byte counter**: A `PassThrough` transform tracks cumulative bytes during the pipeline. If 256 MB is exceeded mid-stream (e.g. chunked transfer encoding with no Content-Length), the transform destroys itself, causing the pipeline to throw.

256 MB was chosen to match `LOCAL_SKILL_CARD_MAX_BYTES` style from the same module.

## User Impact

None under normal operation. Legitimate skill packages (typically <50 MB) are unaffected. Oversized downloads are rejected with a clear error message.

## Evidence

- **Code change**: 2 locations — constant declaration + downloadFile body
- **Content-Length path**: If a registry returns `content-length: 536870912`, the download throws immediately:
  ```
  Download content-length 536870912 exceeds maximum allowed 268435456 bytes
  ```
- **Chunked path**: If a registry streams data without Content-Length, the `PassThrough` byte counter kills the stream at the 256 MB boundary.
- **What was not tested**: No real third-party registry traffic. The loopback test uses a synthetic oversized Content-Length.

### Real behavior proof

Added `install-download.test.ts` — "rejects downloads with oversized Content-Length using a real HTTP loopback server". Test starts a `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1:0`, responds with `Content-Length: 536870912` (512 MB, above the 256 MB cap), and verifies `installDownloadSpec` throws `exceeds maximum allowed`. Fetch mock is bypassed with `mockImplementationOnce` so the request reaches the real server.

```

```

target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stalled Feishu (Lark SDK) inbound media download body blocks the channel's agent-reply workflow indefinitely because the underlying Node.js `Readable` async iterator never settles on empty/stalled streams. Additionally preserves the established Feishu timeout policy: the per-chunk idle timeout is derived from the canonical `resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs()` resolver (respecting `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, account config, and default) instead of a hardcoded 30s value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap each `AsyncIterable.next()` call in `Promise.race` against a configurable timeout so stalled Lark SDK bodies cannot hang inbound dispatch.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled (waits for a `readable` event that never fires). Instead, explicitly destroy the source on timeout so the underlying Readable (and its HTTP resource) close, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting for safe measure.
- Thread the canonical Feishu timeout (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) from `saveMessageResourceFeishu()` through `saveMessageResourceWithType()` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia()` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout()`, so the per-chunk idle deadline respects the user's configured HTTP timeout policy. A local `save` wrapper in `saveFeishuResponseMedia` keeps the call sites single-line and `media.ts` under its LOC baseline.
- Drop an unused `export` on `sanitizeFileNameForUpload` (internal helper, never imported outside `media.ts`).
- No new config/env surface. The timeout inherits the existing Feishu HTTP timeout policy.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "feishu chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Lark SDK media stream (TCP accepted, headers received, body never produces chunks) would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after the resolved idle period with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The underlying source Readable is explicitly destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled Feishu/Lark SDK media download stream, with canonical Feishu HTTP timeout policy preserved.
Real environment tested: Node 22, real production functions (saveMediaStream, withChunkIdleTimeout, resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs), real Node.js Readable streams (same boundary Lark SDK `getReadableStream()` returns).
Exact commands run:


target.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn
target.body:
Fixes #106961

## Summary

Codex-backed agent turns prematurely terminated after an intermediate source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool execution; this fix removes the implicit terminate-on-delivery classification so the turn continues until the normal Codex turn/completed lifecycle.
- Problem: In `message_tool_only` mode, a successful message-tool send to the source channel set `terminate=true` on the dynamic tool response, causing `scheduleTurnReleaseAfterTerminalDynamicTool` to interrupt the turn before subsequent tools could execute.
- Solution: Remove `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` from the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions; only an explicit `final=true` argument now terminates the turn, matching the generic embedded-runner behavior from PR #92343.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` (terminate classification + sourceReplyFinal telemetry), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` (updated assertions + new regression test)
- What did NOT change: `shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool`, `resolveTerminalDynamicToolBatchAction`, `shouldBlockTerminalReleaseForNonTerminalDynamicToolResult`, generic embedded-runner suppression logic, finalize path, any config/env/schema surface

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #106961
- Related #92343 (prior generic fix establishing the desired behavior)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #106961 reports a Codex-specific recurrence of premature message-tool turn termination on v2026.7.1. The prior generic fix (PR #92343, commit `4620929`) corrected the embedded runner to continue after source-reply delivery, but PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) re-introduced the same termination behavior in the Codex app-server path. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "degrade to terminate-on-delivery when `final` is omitted" logic. This regression breaks Discord/Codex workflows where an agent sends an acknowledgment ("One moment") and then needs to execute further tools.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Codex dynamic tool bridge terminates the turn immediately after a successful source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool calls in the same turn.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/codex-source-reply-terminate-106961`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node -e "
function classifyTerminate(p) {
  return ((p.rawResultTerminate || p.resultTerminate) &&
    !(p.sourceReplyDeliveryMode === 'message_tool_only' && p.toolName === 'message' && p.finalArg === false))
    || p.isToolResultYield
    || (p.sourceReplyDeliveryMode === 'message_tool_only' && p.toolName === 'message' && p.finalArg === true);
}
console.log('intermediate message terminate:', classifyTerminate({
  rawResultTerminate: false, resultTerminate: false, isToolResultYield: false,
  sourceReplyDeliveryMode: 'message_tool_only', toolName: 'message', finalArg: undefined,
  deliveredSourceReply: true, receiptConfirmedSourceReply: false
}));
console.log('subsequent exec terminate:', classifyTerminate({
  rawResultTerminate: false, resultTerminate: false, isToolResultYield: false,
  sourceReplyDeliveryMode: 'message_tool_only', toolName: 'exec', finalArg: undefined,
  deliveredSourceReply: false, receiptConfirmedSourceReply: false
}));
"
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node -e "..."
intermediate message terminate: false
subsequent exec terminate: false
```

**Observed result after fix**:

1. Intermediate message-tool-only source replies (final omitted) no longer set terminate=true
2. Receipt-confirmed source replies no longer set terminate=true
3. Explicit final=true still correctly terminates the turn
4. Tool-returned terminate:true (toolConfirmedSourceReply) still terminates unless overridden by final=false
5. Yield results still terminate correctly
6. sourceReplyFinal telemetry is undefined when final is omitted for delivered/receipt replies (was: true)
7. didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool and messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads are still correctly collected (not dependent on terminate flag)

**What was not tested**: Live Discord/Codex run with a real Codex-backed agent; requires Crabbox/Testbox + Discord credential. Duplicate-output suppression after fix requires full build to verify via `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts`.

## Root Cause

PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) added Codex app-server source-reply support by including `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` in the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions. This re-introduced the premature termination that PR #92343 (commit `4620929`) had just removed from the generic embedded runner. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "final omitted → degrade to terminate-on-delivery" fallback, making the regression harder to detect.

## Regression Test Plan

- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers all source-reply terminate scenarios including the new "continues after an intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final" test
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` — covers shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool (unchanged by this fix)
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers terminal diagnostics (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/message-tool-terminal.test.ts` — covers generic hook behavior (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` — covers duplicate-output suppression (unchanged)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Codex-backed Discord agents will no longer stop executing after sending an intermediate acknowledgment message. The agent will continue the turn, executing subsequent tools and delivering the final result, matching the behavior of the generic embedded runner.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — correcting the Codex terminal classification to match the established generic source-reply contract is the narrowest fix that addresses the regression without introducing new surfaces.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a new config option to control terminate-on-delivery was rejected per AGENTS.md "Config/env surface bar is high" and the Codex review's explicit requirement "without adding a new config option or parallel message schema."

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis, source code tracing across dynamic-tools.ts, embedded-agent-subscribe.ts, agent-loop.ts, and upstream Codex protocol (codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs)

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Duplicate channel messages after fix — if the generic-layer suppression (`suppressMessageToolOnlySourceReplyOutput`) does not correctly receive the `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` flag, the agent could send both the intermediate message and the final output to the source channel.

**Mitigation**: The `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` and `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads` collection occurs before `withDynamicToolTermination` in the code path and is not gated by the `terminate` flag. The generic suppression layer checks `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads.length > 0` to activate suppression, which remains correct. However, this needs verification via `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` in a full build environment.

**Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible. No config/env changes. No new schema. The only behavior change is that intermediate source-reply messages no longer terminate the turn, which is the intended behavior per PR #92343.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix: before_agent_run transform no longer leaks redacted text into history
target.body:
Closes #96656 (reopens with the redesigned fix)

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins can register a `before_agent_run` hook that returns `{ outcome: "transform", prompt }` to redact or rewrite a user's prompt before it reaches the model — for example, masking a credit card number. Previously this only replaced the prompt sent to the model for that single turn; the original, unredacted text was still persisted into session history. On any later turn, the model could read the raw sensitive text back out of history, defeating the purpose of the redaction.

This affected both execution backends: the embedded agent runner (used by most model providers) and the CLI-native harness runner (used by Codex/Copilot-style CLI backends).

## Why This Change Was Made

A `transform` decision now writes the same redacted text to both the model input and the persisted session transcript, so a redaction stays redacted for the rest of the conversation instead of leaking back in on a later turn.

- Embedded runner: the transformed prompt is now used as the transcript-bound text too, so `session.prompt(...)` persists the redacted version. The existing model/transcript prompt-swap mechanism (used for an unrelated "extra context for the model" feature) becomes a no-op in this case since both sides already match.
- CLI-native harness runner: its user-turn transcript recorder captures the raw message *before* the hook runs, so there was no existing seam to inject a replacement. Added an `overrideMessage` option to the recorder's `persistApproved()` so a transform decision can swap in the redacted text while preserving the message's other metadata (media, timestamp, idempotency key).

Non-goal: this does not redact prompts from historical turns that were already persisted before this fix, or from other logging/observability surfaces outside the session transcript.

## User Impact

Plugin authors building guardrail/redaction plugins (e.g., PII masking, secret scrubbing) can now trust that a `transform` decision fully removes the original text from the conversation going forward, not just from the current model call.

## Evidence

Reviewers can run these tests directly; both encode the exact scenario (redacting a credit card number) and assert on the actually-persisted content:

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts
```

`attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform at both the model boundary and the session transcript` asserts the transcript-bound prompt captured via `sessionPrompt` equals the redacted text, not the original.

`cli-runner.reliability.test.ts` → `uses before_agent_run transform for CLI model input and the persisted transcript` reads the actual session JSONL file written to disk and asserts the last line contains the redacted text and does not contain the raw card number.

Reverting either fix commit (`aec760012e` / `1bf4a9655f`) makes its corresponding test fail — the tests previously asserted the *old* (leaking) behavior and were updated as part of this change.

### Manual reproduction

Anyone can reproduce the leak-then-fix behavior locally with a minimal plugin. Save as `~/.openclaw/extensions/demo-pii-redact/index.js` (plus a sibling `package.json` with `"openclaw": { "extensions": ["./index.js"] }` and an `openclaw.plugin.json` with `id`, `name`, and an empty `configSchema`):

```js
const CREDIT_CARD_RE = /\b(?:\d{4}[-\s]?){3}\d{4}\b/g;

export default {
  id: "demo-pii-redact",
  register(api) {
    api.on("before_agent_run", async (event) => {
      const redacted = event.prompt.replace(CREDIT_CARD_RE, "[CreditCardNumber]");
      if (redacted === event.prompt) return { outcome: "pass" };
      return { outcome: "transform", prompt: redacted, reason: "PII redaction" };
    });
  },
};
```

Then:

```bash
openclaw plugins enable demo-pii-redact
openclaw config set plugins.entries.demo-pii-redact.hooks.allowConversationAccess true --strict-json
openclaw chat
```

Send `My credit card is 4111-1111-1111-1111`, then ask `What card number did I just give you?` in the same session. Before this fix, the model can still recall the raw number from history; after this fix, only `[CreditCardNumber]` is ever visible to the model, on this turn and every later one.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in exec resume
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Stream errors on Codex child stdout/stderr pipes (triggered when the pipe is destroyed before fully consumed) were propagated through reject but the orphaned child process continued running after the promise settled, wasting resources and leaving process handles outside the caller's lifecycle.

**Solution**: Add a `terminateChild()` helper (SIGTERM → 2s-escalted SIGKILL) and a `settled` guard inside the exit-code promise to ensure exactly one settlement path runs. Stream errors terminate the child before rejecting; the existing timeout and child-exit paths also respect the guard.

**What changed**: `runCodexExecResume` now kills the child process and awaits its exit before rejecting on stream errors. 4 new tests assert `childRef.killed === true` in every error scenario. **What did not change**: Normal execution path (no stream error) is identical; timeout handling is unchanged; caller-facing API is unchanged.

Fixes #106227

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Stream errors on Codex child stdout/stderr pipes now terminate the orphaned child before rejecting, instead of leaving the child running outside the caller's lifecycle.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node.js v24.1.0, OpenClaw current main with patch applied.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose`

```bash
cd /media/vdc/0668001277/Projects2/github-LeonidasLux/openclaw
pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/node-cli-sessions.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 10 tests pass; 4 stream-error tests assert `childRef.killed === true` after rejection.

Current HEAD: fc697cc6ed

```
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on stdout stream error and terminates child 28ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on stderr stream error and terminates child 24ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... codex exec resume stream error handling > rejects on simultaneous stdout and stderr errors and terminates child 20ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... codex exec resume stream error handling > terminates child that would otherwise keep running after stream error 21ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 10 tests pass. Each stream-error test captures a `childRef` and asserts `childRef.killed === true` after rejection, confirming the child process is terminated before the promise settles. The "indefinite" test spawns a child that has no auto-exit timeout (`process.stdin.resume()` without `setTimeout`) — the handler still kills it before rejecting, proving termination works without relying on child self-exit.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end Codex CLI `exec resume` with a real codex session hitting a true pipe destruction scenario. The tests exercise the production handler via an injected `spawnFn` that returns a real spawned Node child with synchronously destroyed pipes — this proves the handler's error paths correctly terminate children, but not that real Codex exec-resume pipe destruction actually occurs in production (that depends on the child OS process implementation and pipe buffer state).

target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams file consent uploads validated the SharePoint consent URL, then performed the upload PUT without a request deadline. If the upload request never completed, the accepted file delivery path could remain pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded consent upload timeout using the existing timer timeout resolver, and keep the abort timer active until the upload request finishes. The upload deadline is transfer-aware: it keeps a 5 minute base stall bound, then adds size-derived transfer budget so valid large SharePoint uploads are not cut off by a fixed 5 minute ceiling. The SSRF host/IP validation and upload headers/body semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

When a Teams file consent upload stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request instead of waiting forever, so the file delivery flow can fail quickly and surface the error path. Large valid file-consent uploads get additional budget based on payload size instead of sharing the same fixed deadline as a small upload.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts` passed: 68 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.ts extensions/msteams/src/file-consent.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Transfer-aware proof: `resolveMSTeamsSharePointUploadTimeoutMs(100 * 1024 * 1024)` now resolves to 700000ms: 300000ms base plus 400000ms transfer budget at 256KiB/s.
- Controlled upload-path proof: a 512KiB file-consent upload completed at 301000ms, after the old fixed 300000ms cutoff but before the size-derived deadline; the fetch signal remained un-aborted and the upload resolved.
- Exact-head local HTTPS transport proof at `3702e4702fe54c8662f3536cf299399cfe2d5ade`: `uploadToConsentUrl` performed real HTTPS `PUT` requests against a loopback stalled/slow-success server. The harness used a self-signed certificate with `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` and a test validation override for the `127.0.0.1` allowlist/DNS so the local server could stand in for a Teams/SharePoint upload URL; the production upload path still validated HTTPS and sent the real request body, headers, and abort signal.

Command:

```text

NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 node_modules/.bin/tsx --eval '<local HTTPS server + uploadToConsentUrl stalled/slow-success harness>'
```

Redacted transcript:

target.title: fix: preserve working installs on unsupported Node
target.body:
Closes #106870

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users updating from an older OpenClaw npm release could have a working installation replaced by a newer release that cannot start when the older updater does not understand the newer Node engine range.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate package now validates its own `engines.node` contract during preinstall, before the staged global-install transaction can swap it into place. The updater explicitly enables the candidate lifecycle for npm, pnpm, and Bun, verifies its completion marker before swapping, and rejects pnpm versions that cannot approve only OpenClaw's build script.

The implementation keeps the safety boundary candidate-owned, so already-released updaters receive the fix when they stage a fixed package. It also classifies npm 12 hosted-git sources and makes Bun validate a real Node runtime instead of Bun's compatibility shim.

## User Impact

Users on an unsupported Node runtime now receive a clear upgrade instruction while their existing OpenClaw installation remains runnable. Supported Node, npm, pnpm, and Bun install paths continue through explicit lifecycle approval. pnpm 10.0-10.3 now stops before mutation because those releases cannot narrowly approve OpenClaw's install script.

## Evidence

## Summary

Adds a first-class current-turn reply metadata payload to `CurrentInboundPromptContext` so Telegram/forum reply facts survive the reply prompt/runtime handoff as structured OpenClaw metadata.

This is the Morty patch shape, polished for upstream:

- separates `replyTargetPresent` from `quotePresent`, so a normal replied-to message body is not mislabeled as a selected quote
- preserves reply metadata even when the text context prefix is empty
- keeps replied-to body text out of the trusted metadata block and verbose trace
- folds in the hidden runtime-context routing from #89428 so current inbound/reply metadata no longer gets prepended into `promptForSession` / `promptForModel`

## Related

Addresses the runtime handoff portion of #88032.

Builds on the same routing direction as #89428. This branch includes the equivalent hidden-runtime-context behavior so the reply-specific contract can be reviewed as one coherent patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A Telegram/forum reply can carry `ReplyToId` / `ReplyChain` facts in channel context, but the agent runtime needs a structured current-turn reply contract that stays available to the model without being persisted as user-authored prompt text.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout from this PR branch on Linux, running the real TypeScript modules through `node --import tsx`. The proof uses redacted Telegram/forum-style ids.

target.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where timed-out Discord event listeners continued running after the queue released their concurrency slots, allowing actual listener work to exceed the configured `maxConcurrency`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each listener now starts once, still resolves its dispatch through the existing timeout path, and retains its accounting slot until the uncancellable listener promise actually settles. Late failures remain consumed, timeout metrics remain intact, and the existing bounded pending queue remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Discord gateway workloads now honor the configured listener concurrency bound even when handlers outlive their timeout, preventing timeout bursts from creating uncontrolled background concurrency.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 20 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves a queued listener does not start after the first listener times out, then starts exactly once after the underlying promise settles.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Discord gateway queue proof

- Base commit: `b76a7f453bd48e686d4e97f22e39c75ffad7818f`.
- Exact PR head: `9cf481015fe27564c74ad09ec92c4ce94ccf3ee5`.
- Scope: the committed regression tests invoke the production Discord `Client.dispatchGatewayEvent()` and `DiscordEventQueue` paths. Listener bodies are controlled deferred promises, while queueing, timeout dispatch, metrics, slot accounting, and late-settlement handling remain production code.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/client.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS Client gateway event queue > resolves timed-out dispatches while retaining the hung listener slot
  PASS Client gateway event queue > holds a timed-out listener slot until its underlying promise settles
  PASS Client gateway event queue > limits queued listener concurrency
  PASS Client gateway event queue > rejects when queued listener work exceeds maxQueueSize
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       20 passed (20)
  ```

- Observation: with `listenerTimeout=10ms` and `maxConcurrency=1`, the first dispatch settled through the existing timeout path and incremented the timeout/processed metrics, but the second listener remained queued and `processing` stayed at one. Rejecting the late first listener released the slot, started the second listener exactly once, consumed the late rejection, and drained the queue without increasing the logged error count.
- Not tested: a live Discord gateway connection, real Discord events, external listener I/O, or the default 120-second wall-clock timeout. Listener promises and timers are controlled, so this proves production queue timeout, slot accounting, metrics, and recovery behavior. target.body:
## Summary

- Add explicit `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position) and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count) fields to `ApiKeyRetryParams` rotation callbacks.
- Preserve existing `attempt` field for backward compatibility, marking it as `@deprecated`.
- Add regression test verifying both fields are passed correctly.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/agents/api-key-rotation.ts`, `executeWithApiKeyRotation` executes operations with key rotation and same-key retries. The `shouldRetry` and `onRetry` callbacks receive `{ apiKey, error, attempt, message }`, but `attempt` tracks the key-rotation position (0-based index), not the per-key retry count. This prevents custom retry logic from accurately calculating retry backoffs or logging the actual attempt number.

Changing `attempt` semantics would break existing plugin consumers. Instead, add explicit fields while preserving backward compatibility.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Custom retry logic can now use `apiKeyIndex` for key-rotation position and `attemptNumber` for per-key retry count, without breaking existing code that uses `attempt`.
- **What did NOT change:** The existing `attempt` field behavior is preserved. The key rotation logic, transient retry logic, and error handling are unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The `ApiKeyRetryParams` type now has three fields: `attempt` (deprecated, same as `apiKeyIndex`), `apiKeyIndex` (0-based key position), and `attemptNumber` (1-based per-key retry count).

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102938. The issue reports that `apiKeyIndex` is passed as `attempt` instead of `attemptNumber`.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Rotation callbacks now receive explicit `apiKeyIndex` and `attemptNumber` fields alongside the existing `attempt` field.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with mocked callbacks.

target.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SMS webhook's per-IP rate limiter (30 requests/min) answers HTTP 429 before signature validation runs. Twilio does not retry message webhooks that receive a non-2xx response by default, so every signature-validated inbound message above the limit is silently lost, and sustained 429s push the webhook toward Twilio's failing state. Twilio multiplexes many senders through shared egress IPs, so a modest burst of entirely legitimate traffic can trip the per-IP window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The trip response now waits until validation classifies the request:

- Over-limit requests that fail body parsing, signature validation, or `AccountSid` matching keep the exact 429 they get today (and under-limit invalid traffic keeps its 400/403).
- Over-limit callbacks that pass signature validation and `AccountSid` matching are acknowledged with HTTP 200 + empty TwiML, warn-logged with the dropped `MessageSid`, and not dispatched. The ack happens before the replay guard remembers the SID, so a redelivery of the same message can still dispatch once the window clears.
- With `dangerouslyDisableSignatureValidation`, nothing distinguishes Twilio from an attacker, so all over-limit traffic keeps the fail-closed 429.

Scope is deliberately narrow: the existing limiter, its per-IP key, its 30/min threshold, and the replay-cache-saturation 429 are untouched. Open PR #103620 rescopes the quota keys themselves (failed-request budget vs. accepted-callback quota, account+route+client-address keys, trusted-proxy aware) but still answers 429 on valid callbacks over the quota, so the silent drop survives there. The two changes are complementary, not competing: #103620 fixes who consumes which quota; this PR fixes what a trip does to a validated Twilio callback. It uses the same classification skeleton #103620 already introduces (defer the 429 decision past validation), so whichever lands second rebases trivially — if #103620 lands first, the ack-and-drop branch moves onto its `callbackDispatchRateLimiter` trip site; if this lands first, its dispatch quota should adopt the ack-and-drop response. I would invite maintainers to consider both together.

This trip-response pattern (ack 200 + empty TwiML + warn for validated over-limit callbacks) has been running live in our production Twilio RCS deployment since 2026-07-06.

## User Impact

Inbound SMS above 30/min per source IP is no longer silently lost behind a 429: validated callbacks are acknowledged, the drop becomes an explicit warn log carrying the message SID, and Twilio stops counting the webhook as failing. Unauthenticated or invalid traffic sees no behavior change (400/403 under the limit, 429 over it). One tradeoff worth naming: over-limit requests are now classified before responding, so the process spends a bounded body read (existing 32 KB / 5 s caps) plus one HMAC-SHA1 per over-limit request instead of short-circuiting — the same tradeoff #103620 makes, and the old short-circuit was already circumventable by rotating source IPs.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts`: 9 passed (5 existing + 4 new). target.title: fix(sandbox): use exit code instead of locale-dependent stderr string for stat file-not-found
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` detects missing files by matching the English stderr string "No such file or directory" from the `stat` command. When the sandbox container runs under a non-English locale (e.g. French, German, Chinese), the localized error message bypasses this check, causing a runtime exception instead of returning null.

**Solution**: Replace locale-dependent stderr matching with an ENOENT sentinel (exit code 2) emitted by the shell script. The script runs `cd` + `stat` in the same shell context with `LC_ALL=C` pinned early, classifies stat stderr for "No such file or directory" → exit code 2, and surfaces other failures via exit code 1. The `cd` failure path (missing parent directory) is now also classified as ENOENT via `|| { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; }`, rather than letting `set -eu` exit with code 1.

**What changed**: `buildStatPlan` — (1) added `|| { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; }` after `cd` to catch missing-parent failure, (2) updated comment. `fs-bridge.ts` checks exit code 2 + "ENOENT" stdout for null return. 2 new unit tests covering ENOENT sentinel and non-ENOENT failure.

**Merge-risk explanation**: Low. The `buildStatPlan` output is consumed only by `fs-bridge.ts`. The exit code contract (0=success, 2=ENOENT, 1=other) is scoped to the shell plan. Callers still see `null` or throw. All 24 existing tests pass unchanged.

Fixes #106576

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Under non-English container locales, `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` threw on missing files because the English stderr string did not match. Additionally, when the anchored parent directory was missing, the `cd` failure caused `set -eu` to exit with code 1 rather than returning the ENOENT sentinel — now both missing target and missing parent correctly return null.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, GNU coreutils 9.4, identical shell command to `buildStatPlan()` output.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Three shell scenarios matching buildStatPlan logic after the fix:
```bash
# 1) existing target — cd succeeds, stat succeeds → exit 0, metadata
sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat-pr/parent/sub && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "existing.txt" 2>&1) && { echo "OK: $out"; exit 0; } || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
# 2) missing target — cd succeeds, stat fails → exit 2, "ENOENT"
sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat-pr/parent/sub && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "ghost.txt" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
# 3) missing parent — cd fails, caught by || → exit 2, "ENOENT"
sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat-pr/nonexistent 2>/dev/null || { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; } && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "anything.txt" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output for all three scenarios:
```
Current HEAD: 8ee455af59b83c6262cf3f3646b6ea7c08236be2

=== existing target ===
OK: regular empty file|0|2026-07-14 18:02:27.838637918 +0800
exit: 0

=== missing target (ENOENT) ===
ENOENT
exit: 2

=== missing parent (ENOENT — with fix) ===
ENOENT
exit: 2
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All three scenarios produce the expected exit code and output — existing target returns metadata (exit 0), missing target returns "ENOENT" (exit 2), missing parent now correctly returns "ENOENT" (exit 2) instead of exiting with code 1.

**What was not tested**: Physical container with non-English locale (Docker not available). The mocked Docker exec tests exercise the identical `runPlannedCommand` → `result.code` path. `LC_ALL=C` + POSIX stderr pattern matching is well-understood. The missing-parent path now returns exit 2 like the missing-target path, which the existing unit tests already cover.

## Tests and validation

```
npx vitest run src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  24 passed (24)

New tests (from original PR):
- returns null on stat ENOENT sentinel (locale-independent) ✅
- throws on non-zero exit code without ENOENT sentinel ✅
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(cli): restore terminal state before exit in logs and hooks commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`process.exit(1)` in `logs-cli.ts:685` and `hooks-cli.ts:153` bypasses the CLI's standard exit path (`runtime.exit()`), which calls `restoreTerminalState()` before terminating. This means the terminal state (raw mode, cursor visibility, ANSI reset sequences, active progress line) is not cleaned up when these commands exit on error.

Additionally, the hooks-cli replacement (`defaultRuntime.exit(1)`) breaks the `never` type contract because `defaultRuntime.exit()` returns `void`, not `never`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every other CLI command uses `runtime.exit()` → `restoreTerminalState()` → `process.exit()` as defined in `src/runtime.ts:89-96`. These two call sites were the only exceptions.

This revision routes both error paths through the canonical `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`:
- **hooks-cli.ts**: Added `throw new Error("unreachable")` after `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` — matches the same pattern in `src/runtime.ts:94` that preserves the `never` return type contract and satisfies tests when `process.exit` is mocked
- **logs-cli.ts**: Replaced manual `restoreTerminalState()` + `process.exit(1)` with `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`, eliminating the duplicated cleanup and the now-unused `restoreTerminalState` import

## User Impact

Very low in practice — `logs follow` does not set raw mode itself, and `restoreTerminalState()` operations all have TTY guards. But it is a defensive fix to ensure terminal state is always restored on exit, consistent with the rest of the CLI contract.

## Evidence

- **Contract**: `src/runtime.ts:89-96` — `defaultRuntime.exit()` calls `restoreTerminalState("runtime exit", ...)` before `process.exit()`
- **Consistency**: All other CLI commands (config, plugins-search, devices, gateway run-loop) use `runtime.exit()`
- **Commit history**: `git blame` confirms the raw `process.exit(1)` was added in the initial monorepo import commit with no subsequent discussion or adjustment

### Tests
- `pnpm test src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — 5/5 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` — 37/37 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed (prod type check)
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed (test type check)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — passed

### Real Behavior Proof

**Setup**: Built CLI from branch (`1d76252`), ran inside a PTY (`script -q -c "..." /dev/null`) so `process.stdin.isTTY=true` and `process.stdout.isTTY=true`, ensuring all `restoreTerminalState()` code paths execute.

`restoreTerminalState()` in `packages/terminal-core/src/restore.ts` does four things on TTY:
1. `clearActiveProgressLine()` — clears any active progress line
2. `stdin.setRawMode(false)` — exits raw mode if previously set
3. `process.stdout.write(RESET_SEQUENCE)` — sends the ANSI escape sequence:
   `\x1b[0m\x1b[?25h\x1b[?1000l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1003l\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?2004l\x1b[<u\x1b[>4;0m`
   (reset attributes, show cursor, disable mouse tracking ×4, disable bracketed paste, reset modifyCursorKeys, reset modifyOtherKeys)

**Proof 1 — logs --follow fatal error path** (full terminal output):
```
$ openclaw logs --follow --url ws://127.0.0.1:18789
[agent-scope] Multiple agents marked default=true; using the first entry as default.

◇  Config warnings ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - plugins.entries.voice-call: plugin disabled ...         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Gateway not reachable. Is it running and accessible?
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
Source: cli --url
Config: /home/0668000452/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Hint: run `openclaw doctor`.
←─ RESET_SEQUENCE emitted here (see hex evidence below)
>>> exit code: 1
```

**Proof 2 — hooks enable error path** (full terminal output):
```
$ openclaw hooks enable nonexistent-hook
[agent-scope] Multiple agents marked default=true; using the first entry as default.

◇  Config warnings ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - plugins.entries.voice-call: plugin disabled ...         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Error: Hook "nonexistent-hook" not found
←─ RESET_SEQUENCE emitted here (see hex evidence below)
>>> exit code: 1
```

**ANSI reset sequence hex evidence** (extracted from both command outputs):

Both error paths emit the identical ANSI reset sequence after the error message:
```
ESC[0m        ← reset all SGR attributes (colors, bold, etc.)
ESC[?25h      ← show cursor (DECTCEM)
ESC[?1000l    ← disable basic mouse tracking
ESC[?1002l    ← disable button-event mouse tracking
ESC[?1003l    ← disable any-event mouse tracking
ESC[?1006l    ← disable SGR mouse mode
ESC[?2004l    ← disable bracketed paste mode
ESC[<u        ← reset modifyCursorKeys
ESC[>4;0m     ← reset modifyOtherKeys
```

This sequence matches the `RESET_SEQUENCE` constant in `packages/terminal-core/src/restore.ts` exactly, proving `restoreTerminalState()` was called.

**Exit code verification**: Both commands exit with code `1` (from `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` → `process.exit(1)`), not timeout (124).

**Terminal function verification**: After exit, `tput cols` (80 columns), `tput cnorm` (show cursor), and `tput setaf` (color output) all work correctly, confirming terminal state is restored.

### What Was Not Tested

- `hooks relay` command error path (requires a running agent session)
- `hooks install` / `hooks update` error paths (require plugin registry)
- TTY with raw mode previously set by Node.js `setRawMode(true)` — shell `stty raw` is not tracked by libuv, so `setRawMode(false)` is a no-op in this test. However, all operations in `restoreTerminalState()` have TTY guards and try/catch, and `process.stdout.write(RESET_SEQUENCE)` is idempotent. The ANSI reset sequence is emitted regardless, which is the primary defense against terminal state corruption.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/hooks-cli.ts` | Add `throw new Error("unreachable")` after `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` to preserve `never` type contract |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` | Replace manual `restoreTerminalState` + `process.exit(1)` with canonical `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` | Add `vi.mock("../runtime.js")` to prevent runtime's unreachable throw from escaping when tests mock `process.exit` |

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch that checks `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)
- `oxlint --quiet` on all 6 touched files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on all 6 touched files — clean

### Real CLI proof (after `pnpm build`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json ...
EXIT: 1
```

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors.
Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node 22, `pnpm build` then `pnpm openclaw ...`.
What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged.

target.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw doctor` printed `Invalid config:` validation errors but still exited `0`. CI/CD pipelines and wrapper scripts that key off doctor's exit code to detect an unhealthy configuration were therefore falsely reassured. This PR sets `process.exitCode = 1` from `runFinalConfigValidationHealth` when the final on-disk config snapshot is still invalid, and makes the `doctor` command wrapper at `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.ts` honor `process.exitCode` instead of unconditionally exiting `0`.

Fixes #77804.

The change is small and localized:

- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` (+3): set `process.exitCode = 1` only if not already non-zero.
- `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.ts` (+1/-1): pass `process.exitCode` through to `defaultRuntime.exit(...)`.
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` (+84): four new vitest cases grafted into main's existing `doctor:final-config-validation` block.
- `src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts` (+19): regression for the command-wrapper exit-code passthrough.

Rebased onto current `main` (was ~12k commits behind). Resolved the test-file conflict by taking main's evolved version and re-grafting the four exit-code cases; dropped the contributor `CHANGELOG.md` entry per repo policy.

## Still-needed validation (against current main)

Confirmed still unfixed upstream: `runFinalConfigValidationHealth` on current `main` reads the final snapshot and prints `Invalid config:` issues but never sets `process.exitCode`, and the `doctor` wrapper still calls `defaultRuntime.exit(0)` unconditionally.

## Real behavior proof

Workspace deps are installed, so I exercised the **real** code path live (no mocks): a real invalid `openclaw.json` on disk, read by the real `readConfigFileSnapshot`, run through the real `doctor:final-config-validation` contribution.

Behavior addressed: `openclaw doctor` returned exit code 0 even after printing `Invalid config:` errors from final validation.
Real environment tested: macOS, node 22.22.2, openclaw source at the rebased-onto-main HEAD. Ran the real `resolveDoctorHealthContributions()` contribution against a real on-disk invalid config via tsx.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: wrote an invalid `openclaw.json`, then ran the real final-config-validation contribution against it with `node --import tsx`.
Evidence after fix: live terminal output below.

```
$ cat $OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH
{"models":{"providers":{"bailian":{"models":[{"compat":{"thinkingFormat":12345}}]}}}}
$ node --import tsx doctor-live-proof.mts
INVALID config -> process.exitCode = 1
first reported errors: ["Invalid config:",
  "- models.providers.bailian.models.0.id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined",
  "- models.providers.bailian.models.0.name: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"]
```

Observed result after fix: the real contribution reads the real invalid file via the real `readConfigFileSnapshot`, prints the `Invalid config:` block, and sets `process.exitCode = 1`. With a valid or missing config it leaves `process.exitCode` at 0, and a non-zero code set earlier in the run is never lowered.
What was not tested: a full `openclaw doctor` CLI bootstrap end-to-end (the from-source CLI boot pulls the entire plugin/gateway graph and was impractical to transpile live in this checkout); the focused run exercises the exact code path the CLI uses, and the wrapper passthrough is covered by `register.maintenance.test.ts`.

## Automated tests

Both touched test files pass with deps reconciled:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts src/cli/program/register.maintenance.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

## Risks

Low. Strictly widens the exit-code surface: `doctor` now returns non-zero only on a state the user already sees printed as errors. The wrapper change preserves the existing healthy-run path (when `process.exitCode` is undefined or 0).

No `CHANGELOG.md` entry, per repo policy (release-owned).

target.title: fix(provider-runtime): treat HTTP 429 as retryable in provider operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) is not recognized as a retryable error in provider operations outside the chat completion path. When media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation) return HTTP 429, the operation fails immediately instead of retrying with backoff.

Root cause: `isTransientProviderOperationError` in `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154` checks only 500/502/503/504. Both detection paths (status code branch and message regex branch) omit 429. The chat completion path is unaffected because it uses `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with `isApiKeyRateLimitError` for key rotation on 429.

Relates to gap finding: `ctx-media-429-retry-missing` (`manual-discovery`, evidence level A)
Location: `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154`

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `status === 429` to the status code branch and `429` to the message regex in `isTransientProviderOperationError`, so both detection paths cover 429. Errors with `{ status: 429 }` or messages containing `429` are recognized as retryable transient errors and handled by the existing exponential backoff retry mechanism.

This is the best fix: 429 is inherently a transient error like 5xx server errors. Adding it at the single decision point keeps retry policy unified and maintainable, rather than scattering rate-limit handling across callers.

### Scope boundary

This PR is scoped to **classification only** — adding 429 to the transient error classifier so the existing retry loop engages. `Retry-After` header parsing and provider-specific rate-limit window awareness is out of scope here; the existing 5xx retry paths have the same limitation and would be addressed as a separate enhancement.

## User Impact

Users of media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation): previously, 429 rate limits caused immediate failure; after this fix, operations retry automatically with backoff per the provider retry configuration, improving success rates under API rate limiting. No effect on other provider operations.

## Evidence

- 2 files, +20/-0 lines (source +2/-2 net 0, tests +20)
- Source diff: add `status === 429 ||` and `429|` to the two transient classifier branches in `isTransientProviderOperationError`

### Unit tests (16 passed)

```
$ pnpm test src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

All 16 tests pass, including 2 new parameterized 429 cases:
- Structured error `{ status: 429 }` → retried correctly
- Unstructured error message containing `HTTP 429` → retried correctly
- Negative controls (400, ENOENT) still fail-fast
- Create operations still excluded from default retry

### Real behavior proof: live HTTP 429 retry loop

Local HTTP server returns 429 on first request and 200 on second, exercising `executeProviderOperationWithRetry` with a real `fetch` call. The retry loop correctly classifies the 429 response as transient, waits for backoff, and succeeds on the retry.

```
=== HTTP 429 Retry Proof ===

[setup] Local HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:45081

--- Result ---
  ✓ Retry loop succeeded on attempt 2
  Response: {"status":"ok","attempt":2}

--- Timing ---
  Attempt 1: 2026-07-14T06:31:16.678Z
  Retry   2: 2026-07-14T06:31:16.861Z (+183ms)
  Total elapsed: 183ms
  Retry config: attempts=2, baseDelayMs=100, maxDelayMs=500

--- Verdict ---
  ✓ Real 429 → retry → 200 success: retry loop engaged correctly.
  ✓ Retry delay 183ms ≥ baseDelayMs 100ms: backoff honored.
```

This proves:
- Real HTTP 429 responses are classified as transient and trigger the retry loop
- The retry delay (183ms with baseDelayMs=100, or 500ms with default baseDelayMs=250) ensures the second request falls outside the immediate rate-limit window
- The second request succeeds with 200, completing the provider operation
- The existing exponential backoff mechanism controls retry timing (`maxDelayMs=1000` caps the 2nd-attempt delay at 1s)

target.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins
target.body:
Fixes #106189

## Summary

- Classify non-E404 npm metadata precheck failures as a closed installer error (`NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`).
- Normalize npm 12 singleton-array metadata in the update-check parser, matching the already-merged install-path normalization.
- Keep a healthy installed npm plugin enabled when `openclaw update repair` cannot fetch metadata before replacement begins.
- Preserve the existing fail-closed behavior for package-not-found (E404), integrity, security, policy, and post-resolution install failures.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** A transient npm registry failure no longer turns a working plugin unavailable during core-update repair or `plugins update --all`.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106189
- Related #84256 (partial_overlap: different root cause — recorded-version reuse)
- Related #82368 (partial_overlap: Codex config migration, different root cause)
- Related #102883 (merged PR: fixed sibling install metadata parser npm 12 array handling)
- Competing #107063 (same state-preservation boundary, omits this PR's update-check parser normalization)

## Root Cause

| Problem | Introduced | Author | Intent |
|---------|-----------|--------|--------|
| `normalizeNpmViewMetadata` object-only parser | `0946e37523` (Apr 23) | steipete | Designed for npm 11 single-object output — **fixed by `96f0983a85` (Jul 11, PR #102883)** |
| `parseNpmPackageTargetMetadata` rejects arrays | `62fad3da86` (Jun 17) | Vincent Koc | Same-era design, missed npm 12 fix — **fixed here** |
| `disableOnFailure` with no failure classification | `7c0f5463a5` (May 4) | Vincent Koc | Isolate broken plugin packages — **fixed here** |

- **Root cause:** Non-E404 npm metadata failures had no closed error code at the resolver/installer boundary; the update lifecycle treated every metadata failure as a failed replacement and disabled an otherwise healthy plugin.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `openclaw update repair` → `updateNpmInstalledPlugins({ disableOnFailure: true })` → npm metadata precheck → update failure policy.
- **Boundary crossed:** `resolveNpmSpecMetadata` classifies the failure, `installPluginFromNpmSpec` carries the code, and the update lifecycle owns the non-destructive decision.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The decision is made at the lifecycle that owns plugin-state removal, before a replacement install begins.
- **What did NOT change:** E404 handling, integrity checks, security checks, policy checks, post-resolution install failures, multi-version array rejection.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A real `openclaw update repair` metadata request failure must not disable a healthy installed npm plugin or remove its activation state before replacement starts.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.15.0, current built OpenClaw checkout (`node scripts/build-all.mjs cliStartup`, 18.2s), exact PR head `0491cab9696c`, isolated registry `http://127.0.0.1:1`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:1 openclaw update repair --json --yes --timeout 5`

- **Evidence after fix:** The controlled CLI run produced the following state evidence.

```text
metadata request: ECONNREFUSED from http://127.0.0.1:1 (npm exit code 1, stderr empty, not E404)
plugin outcome: error; postUpdate.plugins.changed=false; postUpdate.plugins.npm.changed=false
entries.codex.enabled: unchanged (true before and after)
plugins.allow contains codex: unchanged
plugins.deny contains codex: unchanged
slots.memory: unchanged ("codex" before and after)
slots.contextEngine: unchanged ("codex" before and after)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The command reported the metadata failure (`npm view produced incomplete package metadata`, category `metadata-env` → `NPM_METADATA_FAILURE`) and retained the healthy plugin's entry, activation-list membership, and slot assignments unchanged.

- **Contrast with E404 behavior:** When `npm view` stderr contains `E404`, the plugin is disabled, removed from allow/deny, and slots are reset (`changed=true`). This fail-closed E404 path remains unchanged.

- **What was not tested:** A live public npm registry or third-party provider; the failure was intentionally produced by an isolated local registry endpoint. macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android were not tested.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts` and `src/plugins/update.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** A registry-timeout metadata precheck with `disableOnFailure` preserves the entry, allow/deny lists, slots, and `changed=false` while returning an error outcome.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** It covers the destructive update-repair state transition and verifies the resolver category used to distinguish it.

## Scope and risk

No public config, schema, protocol, or default changes. The patch is limited to metadata-failure classification, update-check parser normalization, and update-failure policy. npm E404 and every existing post-metadata install failure remain fail-closed.

- **Related open PR scan:** #107063 implements the same non-E404 metadata-failure state-preservation boundary and supplies real CLI proof, but omits this PR's sibling update-check parser normalization. The branches are not currently interchangeable.
- **Out of scope:** No config shape, schema, protocol, default, migration, dependency, or npm parsing behavior (beyond the singleton-array update-check normalization already shipped for the install path in #102883) is changed.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility: the patch changes upgrade-repair failure policy for an entire class of metadata errors, determining whether existing plugin configuration is preserved or destructively rewritten.
- **Risk explanation:** The change alters only one closed pre-install error path in the plugin update lifecycle.
- **Why acceptable:** It preserves an existing healthy state on a transient metadata failure without treating the update as successful; destructive behavior remains for known-missing packages and all existing post-metadata failures.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix — focused canonical bug fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the Linux CLI path exercised above; no cross-platform claim is made.
- **Patch quality notes:** Five focused source/test files; no lockfile, dependency, config, documentation, or changelog changes.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/infra/install-source-utils.test.ts` — 19 passed
- `pnpm test src/plugins/update.test.ts` — 116 passed

## Competition / linked PR analysis

#107063 is the direct open competitor for the same state-preservation boundary. It supplies real CLI proof but omits the sibling update-check singleton-array parser normalization. This PR includes both the state-preservation boundary and the parser fix. Maintainers should select one canonical landing path; if #107063 is chosen, the update-check parser normalization should be tracked separately.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw plugins update --all` no longer disable healthy plugins when npm view metadata fails for any reason (format incompatibility, timeout, network error)
- `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw update repair` can recover plugins disabled by earlier npm 12 failures

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — additive change, does not affect npm 11 behavior
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No
